mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A skull is examined in the dissection hall. Of which region does the ethmoid bone form an important part? [Prof 25]

options.A: Nasal cavity (roof, septum and lateral walls)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ethmoid: cribriform plate (roof of nose), perpendicular plate (upper septum), labyrinth with ethmoidal air cells. superior and middle conchae; orbital plate (lamina papyracea) forms the medial orbital wall.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has an extradural haematoma after a blow over the temple. Which artery, a branch of the maxillary artery. is torn. [Prof 25. CKMC 26. HITEC 26 . KIMS 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Middle meningeal artery (first part of maxillary artery) enters through foramen spinosum; its anterior branch lies under the pterion 4 biconvex extradural haematoma with lucid interval.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon traces a nerve leaving the middle cranial fossa through the foramen rotundum. Which nerve passes through it? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior orbital fissure: 111, IV, VI, Vl, ophthalmic veins. Rotundum: V2. Ovale: V3, lesser petrosal, accessory meningeal artery. Spinosum: middle meningeal artery. Lacerum: greater petrosal (over it).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon lists the structures passing through the foramen magnum. Which artery passes through the foramen magnum. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Foramen magnum: medulla/spinal cord junction, meninges, vertebral arteries, anterior and posterior spinal arteries. spinal roots of Xl, apical and alar ligaments. tectorial membrane.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a head injury, a man bleeds from the ear and has facial palsy and hearing loss; CT shows a fracture through the petrous temporal bone. Which nerve is most likely injured? [HITEC 26. CKMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Petrous fractures: haemotympanum/bloody otorrhoea, CSF otorrhoea, Battle sign," longitudinal (more common) ￿ conductive loss; transverse sensorineural loss and facial palsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces the middle meningeal artery into the skull. Through which foramen does it pass. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Foramen spinosum (greater wing of sphenoid, posterolateral to ovale) transmits the middle meningeal artery and the meningeal branch of V3.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boxer is hit on the side of the head and becomes unconscious after a lucid interval; CT shows an extradural haematoma. Which bony feature is most likely fractured? [QIMS 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pterion." H-shaped junction of frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of sphenoid - the thinnest part of the skull, overlying the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old has a nasal twang, loss of taste on the posterior third of the tongue and cannot shrug his shoulder; MRI shows a lesion at a skull-base foramen. Which foramen is involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Jugular foramen (Vernet) syndrome: IX (taste, gag), X (palate, voice), Xl (trapezius, SCM). With Xll involvement (hypoglossal canal nearby) = Collet-sicard syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis has atlantoaxial instability. Which ligament holds the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Transverse ligament (part of the cruciform ligament) prevents posterior displacement of the dens into the spinal cord; alar ligaments limit rotation; tectorial membrane is the upward continuation of the PLL.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon views the cranial base from above. Which part of the temporal bone separates the middle from the posterior cranial fossa. [BWP 26]

options.B: Petrous part (superior border, attachment of tentorium)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The petrous ridge (with superior petrosal sinus and tentorium attached) divides the middle and posterior fossae," it houses the inner ear, facial canal and carotid canal; apex near foramen lacerum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has a boggy scalp swelling after a blow to the head; two days later both eyes become bruised. Blood in which scalp layer tracks forward into the eyelids? [Prof 24. AMC 26 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The subaponeurotic (4th, "danger") layer extends to the eyelids anteriorly because the frontalis has no bony attachment; blood/pus there causes black eyes. Emissary veins in this layer spread infection to dural sinuses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has a bleeding laceration of the scalp just in front of the ear. Which artery, a terminal branch of the external carotid, supplies this area. [Prof 25. WMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial temporal artery (pulse felt in front of the tragus) runs with the auriculotemporal nerve," biopsied in giant cell arteritis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with an infected scalp wound develops cavernous/dural sinus thrombosis. In which layer of the scalp are the emissary veins located? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The loose areolar (subaponeurotic) layer is the "dangerous area of the scalp": emissary veins connect it with the diploic veins and dural sinuses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During hair transplant surgery, there is heavy bleeding from the anterior scalp near the midline of the forehead. Which artery is most likely injured? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Anterior scalp." supratrochlear and supraorbital (ICA via ophthalmic),. lateral.. superficial temporal; posterior: posterior auricular and occipital (ECA). Scalp vessels bleed profusely because the dense layer holds them open.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon biopsying the superficial temporal artery identifies a nerve running alongside it. Which nerve is it? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Auriculotemporal (V3) ascends with the superficial temporal vessels in front of the ear, supplying the temple, auricle, EAM, TMJ and carrying parotid secretomotor fibres.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student lists the layers of the scalp. Which scalp layer is the periosteum of the skull bones. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SCALP." Skin, Connective tissue (dense, vessels), Aponeurosis (galea), Loose areolar tissue (danger zone), Pericranium (adherent at sutures, so subperiosteal haematoma (cephalhaematoma) is limited to one bone).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man develops fever and headache days after a deep scalp laceration; imaging shows dural venous sinus involvement. Which scalp layer allowed the spread? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Infection in the subaponeurotic layer spreads via valveless emissary veins (through parietal and mastoid foramina) to the superior sagittal and transverse sinuses 4 thrombosis, meningitis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A deep scalp laceration bleeds profusely because the vessels cannot retract. In which layer of the scalp are the main vessels located? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In the dense subcutaneous layer, fibrous septa bind vessel walls and hold them open ￿ profuse bleeding," control by pressure or sutures through the galea.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with facial nerve palsy cannot close his eyelids. Which muscle is affected? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Orbicularis oculi (Vll,. temporal and zygomatic branches): palpebral part closes gently (blinking), orbital part tightly. Levator palpebrae (111) opens the eye. Exposure keratitis follows its paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a facial infection develops cavernous sinus thrombosis. Which vein connects the facial vein with the cavernous sinus via the pterygoid plexus? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Two routes: facial vein ￿ superior ophthalmic vein 4 cavernous sinus; facial vein 4 deep facial vein 4 pterygoid plexus ￿ emissary veins cavernous sinus. Facial veins are valveless.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A plastic surgeon reconstructs the external nose. Which artery provides the main supply to the side of the external nose. [CKMC 25]

options.D: Facial artery (lateral nasal and superior labial branches)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. External nose: facial (lateral nasal, septal branch of superior labial), ophthalmic (dorsal nasal, external nasal) and infraorbital arteries.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient cannot wrinkle his forehead on one side. Which muscle is paralysed? [CKMC 26. CKMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Frontalis (temporal branch of Vll) raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead; it is spared in UMN (supranuclear) facial palsy because of bilateral cortical innervation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A dentist feels a pulse where an artery crosses the lower border of the mandible. Which artery is palpable at the anteroinferior angle of the masseter. [CKMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Facial artery crosses the inferior border of the mandible at the anterior border of masseter, then runs tortuously to the medial canthus (angular artery).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a facelift, the surgeon avoids a branch of the facial nerve crossing the zygomatic arch. Which branch supplies the frontalis. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Temporal (frontal) branch crosses the zygomatic arch superficially 4 frontalis, upper orbicularis oculi, auricular muscles: injury 4 brow ptosis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A one-year-old girl swallows a caustic cleaner and cannot close her lips. Which muscle is affected? [MUL 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Orbicularis oris (buccal and marginal mandibular branches of Vll) closes and purses the lips; buccinator keeps food out of the vestibule.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has a cleft of the upper lip lateral to the philtrum. Failure of fusion of which processes causes cleft lip. [KIMS 26. MUL 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Medial nasal prominences form the intermaxillary segment (philtrum, premaxilla. primary palate); failure to fuse with maxillary prominences 4 cleft lip (uni-/bilateral). Cleft palate = palatal shelves fail to fuse.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boy squeezes a pimple near his nose; days later he develops cavernous sinus thrombosis. By which route does infection spread from the "danger area" of the face. [BWP 26. MUL 25. BWP 25]

options.C: Facial vein ￿ angular vein 4 superior ophthalmic vein 4 cavernous

mcqs.explanation: sinus / Exam Pearl: Facial veins have no valves; infection spreads via angular/ophthalmic veins or deep facial vein-pterygoid plexus. Key note." source wrote facial the route is venous. nerve via angular vein"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with herpes zoster has vesicles on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson sign). Which nerve supplies the skin at the tip of the nose. [MUL 25]

options.D: Ophthalmic nerve (external nasal branch of nasociliary)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created. the source recalled only the stem and answer. The tip and dorsum of the nose are supplied by Vl (external nasal nerve)," Hutchinson sign predicts ocular involvement because the nasociliary nerve also supplies the cornea.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a facial nerve injury, food collects between the teeth and the cheek while chewing. Paralysis of which muscle (and nerve branch) causes this. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Buccinator presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food on the occlusal surface; it is a muscle of facial expression (Vll), not of mastication, though the buccal nerve of V3 pierces it (sensory).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has an asymmetric smile after facial trauma. Which muscle elevates the angle of the mouth in smiling. [KIMS 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Zygomaticus major draws the angle of the mouth up and laterally (smiling); risorius draws laterally; depressor anguli oris lowers it. All are Vll (zygomatic/buccal branches).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 22~year-old girl has swelling of the left face, drooping of the mouth corner, inability to puff her left cheek and an asymmetric smile; she cannot wrinkle her forehead on that side. Which nerve and type of lesion is this. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Whole-face weakness including forehead = LMN (nucleus or nerve, e.g. Bell palsy). Forehead-sparing = UMN (contralateral cortex/internal capsule).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with facial nerve palsy develops a corneal ulcer. Why. [CKMC 26]

options.C: Loss of blinking and eyelid closure (orbicularis oculi)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In Vll palsy corneal sensation (Vl) is intact but the blink (efferent limb) fails and tear secretion may fall 4 exposure keratitis; protect with tape, lubricants or tarsorrhaphy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A doctor feels the pulse of an artery at the lower border of the mandible as the patient clenches the teeth. From which aspect of the external carotid artery does it arise. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ECA anterior branches: superior thyroid, lingual, facial,. posterior: occipital. posterior auricular: medial: ascending pharyngeal; terminal: maxillary and superficial temporal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has facial pain from a lesion in the pterygopalatine fossa. Which nerve carries the general sensory fibres passing through the pterygopalatine ganglion. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Pterygopalatine ganglion: sensory roots from V2 (pass through without synapse), parasympathetic from the greater petrosal (nerve of pterygoid canal) 4 lacrimal, nasal and palatal glands.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with tetanus cannot open his mouth (lockjaw). Spasm of which muscle prevents mouth opening? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Trismus = spasm of jaw elevators (masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid). The lateral pterygoid (with digastric, gravity) opens the mouth; it is also the muscle that protrudes the mandible.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a haematoma in the infratemporal fossa after an inferior alveolar nerve block. Which artery runs through this fossa and may bleed? [LHR 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Maxillary artery (larger terminal branch of ECA) passes deep to the neck of the mandible through the infratemporal fossa into the pterygopalatine fossa: the pterygoid plexus surrounds the lateral pterygoid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomy student traces the boundaries of the temporal fossa on a skull. What forms its superior (upper) boundary. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Temporal fossa." above and behind - temporal lines; below - zygomatic arch (laterally) and infratemporal crest of greater wing of sphenoid; contains temporalis. deep temporal vessels/nerves; pterion lies in its floor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a protruded jaw is asked to pull it back. Which muscle retracts (retrudes) the mandible. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Protrusion: lateral (and medial) pterygoids. Retrusion: posterior temporalis (+ deep masseter, digastric, geniohyoid). Elevation: temporalis, masseter, medial pterygoid. Depression: lateral pterygoid, digastric. gravity.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A blow behind the condyle of the mandible causes a deep haemorrhage. Which artery, passing deep to the neck of the mandible, is injured? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Maxillary artery arises behind the neck of the mandible within the parotid and runs forward deep to it (with the auriculotemporal nerve above) into the infratemporal fossa.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A dentist blocks the long buccal nerve to anaesthetize the buccal gingiva of lower molars. Where is the buccal nerve approached? [WMC 25]

options.A: Retromolar fossa, at the anterior border of the ramus

mcqs.explanation: Buccal (sensory) branch of V3 emerges between the two heads of lateral pterygoid and crosses the anterior border of the ramus near the retromolar fossa: it supplies cheek skin and mucosa (buccinator is supplied by Vll).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man yawns widely; his jaw dislocates forward and stays open. Which ligament normally prevents anterior (and posterior) dislocation of the temporomandibular joint? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Lateral TM ligament (thickened lateral capsule) is the true ligament of the TMJ. In dislocation the condyle slips in front of the articular eminence and is held by spasm of masseter/temporalis," reduce by pressing down and back on the molars.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A violinist clenches his teeth hard while playing. Which muscle is mainly used to clench the jaw. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Elevators: masseter (most powerful), temporalis, medial pterygoid: all supplied by V3. Masseter hypertrophy occurs with bruxism.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man receives a blow to the angle of the mandible. Which muscle attached to the lateral surface of the angle is affected? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Masseter inserts on the lateral surface of the ramus and angle; medial pterygoid on the medial surface of the angle (pterygomasseteric sling).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old girl cannot close her mouth after yawning; X-ray shows bilateral TMJ dislocation. Which muscle pulls the condyle forward over the articular eminence. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Lateral pterygoid inserts into the neck of the condyle and the articular disc and pulls them forward in opening; excessive opening dislocates the condyle anteriorly, then elevator spasm locks it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Two days after removal of an impacted lower third molar, a man has numbness of the right lower lip and chin. Which nerve is injured? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Inferior alveolar nerve (V3) runs in the mandibular canal close to third molar roots; its mental branch emerges at the mental foramen (below the 2nd premolar) to supply the lower lip and chin.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During extraction of a mandibular third molar, the patient later has numb anterior tongue on that side. Which nerve is at risk lingual to the third molar. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The lingual nerve lies directly against the periosteum lingual to the third molar, just below the mucosa; the inferior alveolar nerve is related to the roots within the canal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A dentist needs to anaesthetize the lower premolars. Which artery supplies the mandibular premolars. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior alveolar artery (1st part of maxillary) enters the mandibular foramen with the nerve and supplies all lower teeth,. the mental artery emerges at the mental foramen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces nerves in the infratemporal fossa. Which nerve emerges at the lower border of, and runs medial to, the lateral pterygoid? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Branches of V3 at the lateral pterygoid: buccal between its heads." masseteric and deep temporal above," lingual and inferior alveolar below/medial (on the medial pterygoid),. chorda tympani joins the lingual here.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon traces the maxillary artery into the pterygopalatine fossa. Which is its terminal branch? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Maxillary artery." 1st part (mandibular) - middle meningeal, inferior alveolar; 2nd (pterygoid) - muscular," 3rd (pterygopalatine) - posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital, descending palatine, sphenopalatine (terminal).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces the communications of the pterygopalatine fossa. Through which pathway does the fossa communicate with the region of the foramen lacerum. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pterygopalatine fossa." foramen rotundum (middle cranial fossa). pterygoid canal (foramen lacerum - nerve of pterygoid canal), sphenopalatine foramen (nose), inferior orbital fissure (orbit). pterygomaxillary fissure (infratemporal fossa), palatine canals (palate).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A dentist asks which muscle inserts on the coronoid process. Which muscle attaches to the coronoid process of the mandible. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Temporalis inserts into the coronoid process and anterior ramus (elevation, retraction); masseter into lateral ramus/angle; medial pterygoid into medial angle; lateral pterygoid into condylar neck and disc. NECK)

mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A diabetic has a deep neck infection that spreads from behind the pharynx into the posterior mediastinum. Which space allows infection to spread from the neck into the thorax. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: . Retropharyngeal space (between buccopharyngeal and alar fascia) reaches the superior mediastinum (~T2); the danger space (between alar and prevertebral fascia) extends to the diaphragm.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A patient cannot shrug his shoulder after a lymph node biopsy in the posterior triangle. Which cranial nerve is injured? [Prof 25. AMC 26. KIMS 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Spinal accessory nerve crosses the posterior triangle superficially on levator scapulae (below the investing fascia roof), vulnerable in node biopsy trapezius paralysis, shoulder droop.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old has a small opening discharging mucus at the anterior border of the lower sternocleidomastoid. Persistence of which embryological structure causes this. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Second arch overgrows the 2nd-4th clefts forming the cervical sinus; remnants 4 branchial cyst (angle of mandible, anterior to SCM) or sinus/fistula opening along the anterior border of SCM.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A child has a retropharyngeal abscess. Between which layers of deep cervical fascia is the retropharyngeal space located? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Retropharyngeal space." between buccopharyngeal fascia (behind the pharynx) and alar fascia. Danger space: between alar and prevertebral fascia. Prevertebral space: behind the prevertebral fascia (Pott abscess).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A surgeon ligates the superior thyroid artery at the upper pole. From which artery does it arise. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: ECA branches: superior thyroid, ascending pharyngeal, lingual. facial, occipital, posterior auricular. maxillary, superficial temporal ("Some Anatomists Like Freaking Out Poor Medical Students").

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A man with an apical lung tumour has drooping of the upper eyelid, a small pupil and a dry face on one side. Which nerve pathway is damaged? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Horner syndrome: ptosis (Muller muscle), miosis, anhidrosis, enophthalmos interruption of the oculosympathetic pathway (hypothalamus 4 TI superior cervical ganglion 4 ICA plexus). Key note: source keyed facial nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A deep neck infection spreads rapidly to the diaphragm. Between which fasciae does the "danger space" lie. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Danger space (space 4) extends from the skull base to the posterior mediastinum/diaphragm because it has no inferior fusion of fascia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old has a carcinoma at the tip of the tongue. To which lymph nodes does the tip drain first? [HITEC 26. BWP 26. MUL 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Tip 4 submental," marginal anterior 2/3 4 submandibular." central 4 deep cervical (bilaterally)." posterior 1/3 4 jugulodigastric (bilateral). Jugulo-omohyoid is the "lymph node of the tongue"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A tonsillar infection spreads lateral to the pharynx toward the carotid sheath. Into which space does a lateral pharyngeal abscess spread? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Parapharyngeal space: inverted cone from skull base to hyoid. lateral to superior constrictor, contains carotid sheath (post-styloid compartment)," infection 4 trismus, carotid erosion, IJV thrombosis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: During neck surgery, bleeding occurs from the deep cervical artery. Which vessel gives rise to the deep cervical artery. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Costocervical trunk (2nd part of subclavian) 4 deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries. Thyrocervical trunk ￿ inferior thyroid, suprascapular. transverse cervical.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: After ligation of one external carotid artery, the face and neck remain well perfused. Through which pathway is collateral supply maintained? [WMC 25]

options.C: Anastomoses across the midline with branches of the opposite ECA

mcqs.explanation: (e.g. facial, thyroid arteries) / Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Free anastomoses between right and left ECA branches (facial, lingual. superior thyroid) and with ICA (ophthalmic) and subclavian (inferior thyroid) maintain supply; ECA can be ligated safely.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A surgeon outlines the carotid triangle before exposing the carotid bifurcation. What forms its lateral (posterior) boundary. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Carotid triangle: SCM (posterolateral), posterior belly of digastric + stylohyoid (superior), superior belly of omohyoid (anteroinferior). Contains carotid bifurcation, IJV, X, Xll, ansa cervicalis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A carcinoma of the posterior third of the tongue spreads to lymph nodes. To which nodes does the posterior third drain. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Posterior third and central parts drain bilaterally - hence bilateral neck dissection may be needed for posterior tongue cancers.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A smoker has a carcinoma of the central part of the lower lip. To which lymph nodes does it drain first? [CKMC 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Upper lip and lateral lower lip 4 submandibular; central lower lip and chin 4 submental. Submandibular nodes also drain the cheek, upper lip, side of nose and anterior tongue.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: During excision of the submandibular gland, the surgeon identifies structures in the submandibular triangle. Which structure lies in this triangle. [HITEC 25]

options.B: Facial artery and vein, hypoglossal nerve and nerve to mylohyoid

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Digastric triangle: submandibular gland and nodes, facial artery and vein, hypoglossal nerve, nerve to mylohyoid, part of parotid; marginal mandibular nerve at risk in the skin incision.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A young adult has a painful fluctuant swelling at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid below the angle of the mandible, with difficulty swallowing. What is the developmental cause? [BWP 25]

options.D: Remnant of the 2nd pharyngeal cleft (cervical sinus) - branchial cyst

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Branchial cyst: lined by squamous epithelium with cholesterol crystals; lies along the anterior border of SCM; a fistula passes between internal and external carotid arteries to the tonsillar fossa.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A 19-year-old has a swollen, tender submandibular lymph node. Which region is most likely the source of infection? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Submandibular nodes drain upper lip, lateral lower lip, cheek, side of nose, medial eyelid angle. anterior tongue, gums and teeth. Lateral eyelids/face ￿ preauricular (parotid); central lower lip, chin 4 submental.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A 32-year-old woman has painless enlarged nodes along the anterior triangle of the neck. Which group of lymph nodes is primarily involved? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. All head and neck lymph ultimately drains to the deep cervical chain along the internaljugular vein tiugulodigastric, jugulo-omohyoid), then the jugular trunk.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man has a hard left supraclavicular node (Virchow node) with weight loss. Which primary cancer is classically associated? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Troisier sign: left supraclavicular node near the termination of the thoracic duct - gastric and other abdominal/pelvic cancers.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A man has high fever and painful swelling along the side of the neck; a deep neck abscess involves the carotid sheath. Which structures lie within the carotid sheath? [BWP 26 . KIMS 25]

options.A: Internal jugular vein and vagus nerve (with carotid artery)
options.B: Internal carotid artery and recurrent laryngeal nerve
options.D: Phrenic nerve and middle cervical ganglion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Carotid sheath contains the common/internal carotid artery (medial), IJV (lateral), vagus (posterior, between them), deep cervical nodes; ansa cervicalis is embedded in its anterior wall; sympathetic trunk lies behind it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A cancer on the right lateral margin of the anterior tongue spreads to the neck. To which nodes does the right side of the anterior tongue primarily drain. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Marginal lymphatics of the anterior 2/3 drain ipsilaterally to submandibular nodes; central lymphatics may cross to both sides.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A man has nasopharyngeal carcinoma. To which lymph nodes does it most commonly spread first? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nasopharynx drains to retropharyngeal then upper deep cervical (and posterior triangle) nodes; NPC often presents with a neck mass, unilateral otitis media with effusion (Eustachian obstruction) and EBV association.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A thyroid swelling moves up with swallowing. Which layer of deep cervical fascia encloses the thyroid gland? [AMC 26. BWP 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pretracheal fascia forms the false capsule of the thyroid and attaches to the cricoid and thyroid cartilages (ligament of Berry) - so the thyroid moves with the larynx on swallowing.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A student traces the axillary sheath upward. Which layer of deep cervical fascia extends into the axilla as the axillary sheath? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl. Prevertebral fascia covers the prevertebral and scalene muscles, brachial plexus roots and subclavian artery and is drawn out laterally as the axillary sheath; it forms the floor of the posterior triangle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: After excision of a right jugular foramen schwannoma, a patient cannot turn his face to the left against resistance. Which nerve was injured? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The right sternocleidomastoid turns the face to the LEFT (and tilts the head to the right).. Xl exits the jugular foramen with IX and X.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A woman with recurrent tonsillitis has a tender enlarged node deep to the sternocleidomastoid below the angle of the mandible. Which node is enlarged? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Jugulodigastric node lies where the posterior belly of digastric crosses the IJV - drains the palatine tonsil and posterior tongue; commonly enlarged in tonsillitis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A man has swelling just below and behind the angle of the mandible from lymph node enlargement. Which nodes are most likely enlarged? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parotid/preauricular nodes drain the lateral face. eyelids, temporal scalp and EAM; infra-auricular parotid nodes lie near the angle. Source location was imprecise.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A student identifies the triangles of the neck. Which triangle has the body of the hyoid bone as its base. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Submental triangle." between anterior bellies of digastric with the hyoid body as base (floor: mylohyoid). Muscular triangle lies below the hyoid. Key note: source keyed muscular triangle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: A student traces the external carotid artery within the parotid gland. What are its terminal branches. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The ECA ends behind the neck of the mandible within the parotid by dividing into the maxillary and superficial temporal arteries.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Vessels & Lymphatic Drainage of Head & Neck (Deep Fascia & Triangles of Neck)
mcqs.question: During parotid surgery, the surgeon identifies a vein formed by the posterior division of the retromandibular vein and the posterior auricular vein. Which vein is it? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EJV forms near the angle of the mandible, crosses the SCM superficially and drains into the subclavian vein," it distends with raised venous pressure (visible JVP is assessed from the IJV).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a dry eye after a temporal bone fracture through the facial canal near the geniculate ganglion. Damage to which nerve causes loss of lacrimation? [Prof 24. AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lacrimal pathway: superior salivatory nucleus 4 Vll 4 greater petrosal 4 nerve of pterygoid canal 4 pterygopalatine ganglion ￿ zygomatic (V2) - lacrimal nerve (Vl) ￿ gland.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has Bell palsy from a lesion at the stylomastoid foramen. What is the effect? [Prof 24. WMC 26. MUL 25]

options.A: Ipsilateral loss of sensation on the face
options.C: Loss of taste on the posterior one-third of the tongue
options.D: Ipsilateral paralysis of the muscles of facial expression only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: At the stylomastoid foramen, the branches for lacrimation (greater petrosal), stapedius (hyperacusis) and taste (chorda tympani) have already left so only facial muscles are paralysed.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has hoarseness, dysphagia and his uvula deviates to the right. Which cranial nerve is affected? [Prof 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagus (CN X) supplies palate, pharynx and larynx muscles (via nucleus ambiguus)," the uvula deviates AWAY from the paralysed side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has lost the gag reflex sensation and taste on the posterior third of the tongue. Which cranial nerve is damaged? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN IX: afferent limb of gag reflex, taste and sensation of posterior 1/3 tongue. carotid sinus/body, parotid secretion, stylopharyngeus. Exits through the jugular foramen with X and Xl.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has numbness of the cheek, lower eyelid and upper lip. Which division of the trigeminal nerve is involved? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vl 4 forehead, upper lid, nose bridge; V2 ￿ cheek, lower lid. upper lip, upper teeth (via foramen rotundum, infraorbital nerve); V3 ￿ lower lip, chin, lower teeth, temporal region and mastication muscles (foramen ovale).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has facial droop, loss of taste on the anterior tongue and hyperacusis. Which cranial nerve is affected (proximal to the stapedius branch)? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lesions of Vll in the facial canal above the nerve to stapedius 4 hyperacusis + loss of taste (chorda tympani) + facial palsy." above the geniculate ganglion ￿ also dry eye.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After middle ear surgery, a man loses taste on the anterior two-thirds of one side of the tongue. Which nerve is damaged? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chorda tympani crosses the medial surface of the tympanic membrane (between incus and malleus handle), exits via the petrotympanic fissure and joins the lingual nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a facial palsy also has hyperacusis and loss of taste on the anterior tongue, but normal tear secretion. Where is the facial nerve damaged? [CKMC 25. HITEC 25]

options.C: In the facial canal between the geniculate ganglion and the nerve to

mcqs.explanation: stapedius / Exam Pearl: Hyperacusis + taste loss = lesion proximal to the nerve to stapedius but distal to the geniculate ganglion (greater petrosal spared ￿ normal tears). Key note: source answered stylomastoid foramen, where only facial muscles are affected.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies cranial sensory ganglia. Which ganglion is formed from both neural crest cells and ectodermal placodes. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ganglia of V, VII, IX. X have neural crest (proximal) and placodal (distal) contributions; the vestibulocochlear ganglion is derived from the otic placode; autonomic ganglia are pure neural crest. Key note: source keyed statoacoustic ganglion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A blow-out fracture injures the infraorbital nerve. Which area loses sensation. [BWP 25]

options.A: Cheek, lower eyelid, side of nose and upper lip

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Infraorbital nerve (V2) runs in the orbital floor groove/canal and exits the infraorbital foramen; also supplies upper anterior teeth (anterior superior alveolar branch).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student identifies the nerve of the second pharyngeal arch. Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: all Vll. 1st arch muscles (mastication, Exam Pearl: 2nd arch derivatives: muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid, posterior belly of digastric mylohyoid, anterior digastric, tensors) - V3.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student lists the special sensory cranial nerves. Which cranial nerve carries the special sense of smell? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CNI." _20 bundles of unmyelinated axons of bipolar olfactory neurons pass through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb (mitral and tufted cells).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient cannot close his right eye or smile on the right, but taste and hearing are normal. Where is the facial nerve lesion? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Facial canal proximal to the geniculate ganglion
options.D: Facial canal proximal to the chorda tympani

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal taste and hearing (no hyperacusis) 4 lesion distal to the chorda tympani and nerve to stapedius, i.e. at/after the stylomastoid foramen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A skull-base fracture causes loss of function of frontalis, orbicularis oculi, orbicularis oris and buccinator on one side. Which nerve is affected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All these muscles of facial expression are 2nd-arch derivatives supplied by Vll: buccinator is a facial-expression muscle even though it aids chewing.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After recovery from a facial nerve palsy, a man sheds tears whenever he eats. Misdirected regeneration of which nerve causes "crocodile tears" syndrome. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Greater petrosal nerve (salivary f ibres regrow into lacrimal pathway)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bogorad syndrome: lesion proximal to the geniculate ganglion 4 fibres destined for submandibular/sublingual glands regrow along the greater petrosal nerve to the lacrimal gland. Compare Frey syndrome (auriculotemporal).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man loses taste from the anterior two-thirds of his tongue. In which ganglion are the cell bodies of these taste fibres. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Taste neurons are pseudounipolar sensory cells: Vll 4 geniculate ganglion; IX ￿ inferior (petrosal) ganglion; X 4 inferior (nodose) ganglion. Submandibular and otic ganglia are parasympathetic.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman develops sweating and flushing over her cheek while eating, months after parotidectomy. Damage to which nerve causes Frey syndrome? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Severed parasympathetic secretomotor fibres in the auriculotemporal nerve regrow into sympathetic fibres of facial sweat glands 4 gustatory sweating.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with mumps has a swollen painful parotid gland. Which nerve carries the preganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the parotid? [Prof 24. AMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parotid: inferior salivatory nucleus 4 IX 4 tympanic nerve (Jacobson) 4 tympanic plexus 4 lesser petrosal 4 otic ganglion 4 auriculotemporal nerve parotid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a stone in Wharton duct causing swelling during meals. Which glands receive postganglionic fibres from the submandibular ganglion. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior salivatory nucleus 4 Vll 4 chorda tympani 4 joins lingual nerve ￿ submandibular ganglion 4 submandibular and sublingual glands. Parotid uses the otic ganglion (IX).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide shows mucous acini capped by serous demilunes. In which gland are these present? [KIMS 26. AMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Submandibular: mixed, mainly serous with serous demilunes (an artefact of fixation); sublingual: mainly mucous,. parotid: purely serous with long intercalated ducts.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon must preserve the secretomotor supply of the submandibular gland during floor-of-mouth surgery. Which nerve carries these fibres to the submandibular ganglion? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chorda tympani preganglionic fibres hitch-hike on the lingual nerve to the submandibular ganglion, which hangs from the lingual nerve on the hyoglossus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist examines a serous gland cell that secretes large amounts of enzyme protein. Which organelle is most abundant in such a protein-secreting cell? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Protein-secreting cells (parotid, pancreatic acini) have basal RER (basophilia), prominent Golgi and apical zymogen granules; steroid cells have abundant SER and mitochondria. Key note." source answered mitochondria.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After parotidectomy, a patient cannot close his eye and the corner of his mouth droops. Which structure was damaged during surgery. [BWP 26. CKMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Facial nerve divides within the parotid (between superficial and deep lobes) into temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical branches; the gland is supplied by IX, not vii.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A dentist sees the opening of the parotid duct in the cheek. Which muscle does the parotid (Stensen) duct pierce. [MUL 25. HITEC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parotid duct crosses the masseter, turns medially at its anterior border. pierces buccal fat and buccinator and opens opposite the upper second molar.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology examiner asks about salivary gland acini. Which statement is correct? [HITEC 25]

options.D: Parotid is purely serous; submandibular mainly serous; sublingual

mcqs.explanation: mainly mucous / Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Parotid: serous. long intercalated ducts, fat cells. Submandibular: mixed (mostly serous) with demilunes, long striated ducts. Sublingual: mostly mucous, short ducts.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has painful swelling of the floor of the mouth during meals; a stone is felt in Wharton duct. Which gland is involved? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. 80A of salivary calculi occur in the submandibular gland: alkaline, viscous mucoid saliva and an upward-running duct. Wharton duct opens on the sublingual papilla.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A slide shows a gland with purely serous acini, intercalated and striated ducts and connective tissue septa. What best describes the secretion of this gland? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Watery serous secretion rich in amylase and ions

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Parotid (purely serous) produces watery, salivary amylase (ptyalin)-rich saliva," striated ducts modify ions (reabsorb Na", secrete K., HCO,-) under aldosterone influence.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has pain beneath her tongue during meals; pressure on the floor of the mouth expresses pus near the lingual frenulum. Where does the submandibular duct open. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Submandibular (Wharton) duct opens on the sublingual caruncle," sublingual gland opens by many small ducts along the sublingual fold (some into the Wharton duct).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide shows purely serous acini, long intercalated ducts and fat cells. Which gland is this. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parotid: purely serous (in adults), long intercalated ducts, many adipocytes, facial nerve branches in the gland; submandibular has long striated ducts and demilunes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomy student locates the sublingual gland. Where does the sublingual gland lie? [CKMC 26]

options.C: In the floor of the mouth, beneath the sublingual fold above

mcqs.explanation: mylohyoid / Exam Pearl: Sublingual gland lies in the sublingual fossa of the mandible above mylohyoid. beneath the mucosa of the sublingual fold; a ranula is a mucous extravasation cyst of this gland.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist sees pale cells inside the acini of a gland, continuous with intercalated ducts. In which organ are centroacinar cells found? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Centroacinar cells (start of intercalated ducts inside the acinus) are unique to the exocrine pancreas and secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid in response to secretin. Salivary glands lack them.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide shows salivary ducts with basal striations. What causes the striated appearance of striated ducts. [HITEC 26]

options.C: Basal infoldings of the plasma membrane with mitochondria

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Striated ducts modify saliva (reabsorb Na., Cl-; secrete K,, HCO,-) using energy from mitochondria in basal infoldings - making saliva hypotonic. They are longest in the submandibular gland.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During superficial parotidectomy, the surgeon traces a vein within the gland down toward the angle of the mandible. Which vein is it? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial temporal + maxillary veins 4 retromandibular vein (within parotid, deep to facial nerve). Its anterior division joins the facial vein (4 IJV)," posterior division + posterior auricular vein ￿ externaljugular vein.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During parotidectomy, the surgeon exposes a muscle in the bed of the gland that runs from the mastoid notch to an intermediate tendon near the hyoid. Which muscle is it? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parotid bed: mastoid process, SCM, posterior belly of digastric, styloid process and its muscles, IJV. ICA, Ix-xll. The facial nerve trunk is found just above the posterior belly of digastric.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has ptosis and his eye rests "down and out" with a dilated pupil. Which cranial nerve is affected? [Prof 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN111 supplies levator palpebrae, SR, IR, MR. 10 and the sphincter pupillae/ciliary muscle; unopposed LR (Vl) and SO (IV) pull the eye down and out.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a blocked tear drainage system has swelling at the medial canthus. On which wall of the orbit does the lacrimal sac lie. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lacrimal sac lies in the lacrimal fossa (lacrimal bone + frontal process of maxilla) on the medial wall,. the nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus (valve of Hasner).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ophthalmologist examines the posterior layer of the cornea under a slit lamp. What is the basement membrane of the corneal endothelium called? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cornea (5 layers)." epithelium (stratified squamous non-keratinized), Bowman layer, stroma (~90% of thickness). Descemet membrane. endothelium (pumps fluid out. does not regenerate).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with an infected boil near the medial canthus develops proptosis, chemosis and ophthalmoplegia. Through which vein does infection reach the cavernous sinus? [KIMS 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Angular vein H superior ophthalmic vein (valveless) ￿ cavernous sinus; CN VI (lying free in the sinus) is usually affected first.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ophthalmology student labels retinal layers. In which layer are the cell bodies of rods and cones located? [CKMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Retina (outside 4 in): pigment epithelium, rods/cones (outer segments), outer limiting membrane, outer nuclear (photoreceptor nuclei), outer plexiform, inner nuclear (bipolar, horizontal, amacrine, Muller), inner plexiform, ganglion cell, nerve fibre layer.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An elderly woman has persistent overflow of tears down her cheek. What is the commonest cause of epiphora in adults. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Epiphora = overflow of tears from impaired drainage (nasolacrimal duct obstruction, punctal eversion, lower lid laxity in Vll palsy). Lacrimation = excess production.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies eye development. The optic vesicle is an evagination of which brain region. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic vesicle (diencephalon) 4 invaginates into optic cup (two-layered: neural retina + pigment epithelium),. lens placode (surface ectoderm) forms the lens; choroidal fissure carries hyaloid artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student measures corneal thickness in histology. Which layer forms the thickest part of the cornea. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stroma: _ 90% thickness. regularly arranged type I collagen lamellae and keratocytes - transparency depends on spacing and deturgescence (endothelial pumps).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has double vision when looking down and in, especially going downstairs. Which nerve is damaged? [MUL 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN IV ￿ superior oblique: depression in adduction, intorsion; palsy 4 vertical diplopia worse on looking down, head tilted away from the affected side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ophthalmologist examines a brown iris. In which ocular structure is melanin abundant and responsible for eye colour. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Melanin in the iris stroma determines eye colour (brown = much, blue = little); pigment epithelium of iris/retina and choroid absorb stray light. Cornea, lens and vitreous are transparent.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A young man develops optic neuritis with deep retro-orbital pain after sinusitis. Infection of which sinus most likely affects the optic nerve. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic canal is related to the sphenoid sinus and posterior ethmoidal cells (Onodi cell) their infection can cause retrobulbar optic neuritis," ethmoid sinusitis most commonly causes orbital cellulitis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ophthalmology student lists the coats of the eyeball. What forms the outer (fibrous) layer of the eye. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Outer fibrous tunic: sclera + cornea," middle vascular tunic (uvea): choroid, ciliary body, iris," inner neural tunic: retina.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man's right eye turns inward and cannot move outward. Which nerve is damaged? [HITEC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LR6 S04 (rest 3).. lateral rectus paralysis 4 medial strabismus (convergent squint) and horizontal diplopia worse on looking to the affected side. CN Vl has the longest intracranial course.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boxer receives a blow to the eye; he cannot look upward, and X-ray shows a fracture of the orbital floor. Which muscle is entrapped? [AMC 26. HITEC 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Blow-out fracture." pressure on the globe breaks the thin orbital floor into the maxillary sinus 4 inferior rectus/fat entrapment (failed upward gaze, diplopia), infraorbital nerve numbness, enophthalmos.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A baby is born with one eye completely absent. Failure of formation of which structure is responsible. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anophthalmia = failure of the optic vesicle to form; microphthalmia = arrested development; cyclopia = holoprosencephaly (SHH defect).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has a keyhole-shaped defect of the iris at its inferior margin. Failure of closure of which structure causes this. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Choroidal fissure normally closes in the 7th week; failure 4 coloboma of iris (+ ciliary body, retina, choroid, optic nerve). Aniridia = PAX6 mutation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 34-year-old has horizontal diplopia and cannot abduct his left eye; other nerves in the region are normal. Where is CN Vl most likely compressed? [QIMS 25]

options.B: Cavernous sinus (lies free beside the ICA)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. CN Vl runs within the cavernous sinus next to the ICA (others lie in its lateral wall), so it is the first affected in cavernous sinus thrombosis or carotid aneurysm.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After orbital trauma, a patient cannot elevate his eye when looking medially; other movements are intact. Which muscle and nerve are affected? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Clinical testing: in adduction, the obliques act as elevator (10) and depressor (SO),. in abduction, the recti act as elevator (SR) and depressor (IR).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After blunt eye trauma, a patient sees a curtain over part of his vision; fundoscopy shows retinal detachment. Which layers separate in retinal detachment? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Neural retina from the retinal pigment epithelium

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. The potential space between the two layers of the optic cup (intraretinal space) persists,. photoreceptors separated from RPE lose their nourishment - urgent repair is needed.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has loss of central vision with intact peripheral vision; fundoscopy shows macular degeneration. Which structure is affected? [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Fovea: only cones, inner layers displaced, highest acuity, supplied by the choriocapillaris (avascular zone). Optic disc = blind spot (no photoreceptors).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old develops periorbital swelling and pain after an upper respiratory infection; imaging shows spread from a sinus into the orbit. Which sinus is most likely involved? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. The lamina papyracea (medial orbital wall) is paper-thin, so ethmoiditis is the commonest cause of orbital cellulitis in children (ethmoid and maxillary sinuses are present at birth).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ophthalmologist examines a patient with anterior uveitis. Which is the most anterior part of the uveal tract? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uvea (vascular tunic) from front to back: iris ￿ ciliary body 4 choroid. Anterior uveitis (iritis) causes a painful red eye with a small irregular pupil.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient's eye cannot look down when turned inward. Which muscle depresses the adducted eye and also intorts it? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SO." intorsion (primary), depression and abduction; best tested by looking down in adduction. IR: depression (best in abduction), extorsion, adduction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces the secretomotor route to the lacrimal gland. Which nerve carries the postganglionic fibres from the pterygopalatine ganglion toward the lacrimal gland? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Postganglionic fibres: pterygopalatine ganglion 4 V2 4 zygomatic nerve 4 zygomaticotemporal 4 communicating branch 4 lacrimal nerve (Vl) gland.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies eye development. From which tissue does the lens develop. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic vesicle induces the overlying surface ectoderm to form the lens placode ￿ lens vesicle. Cornea: surface ectoderm (epithelium) + neural crest (stroma, endothelium). Retina." neuroectoderm.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A section shows a transparent, avascular structure with thick collagenous stroma, lined by epithelium on both surfaces. Identify the structure. [HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cornea: stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium (anterior), Bowman layer. stroma, Descemet membrane. endothelium (posterior). Avascular, richly innervated (Vl), nourished by aqueous and tears.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A tumour is found in the optic canal. Which structure accompanies the optic nerve through the optic canal? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic canal (lesser wing of sphenoid): optic nerve with its meninges + ophthalmic artery (inferolateral). 111, IV, Vl branches, Vl and ophthalmic veins pass through the superior orbital fissure.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After an orbital injury, a man has blurred near vision and a slightly dilated pupil with a sluggish light reflex. The parasympathetic root of the ciliary ganglion is carried by which cranial nerve. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ciliary ganglion: parasympathetic root from111 (EW nucleus) via the nerve to inferior oblique ￿ short ciliary nerves 4 sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle; sympathetic and sensory (nasociliary) fibres pass through without synapse.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a superficial corneal abrasion, the eye heals within 24-48 hours without scarring. Which corneal layer can regenerate. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Epithelium regenerates rapidly from limbal stem cells; Bowman layer does not (scars); endothelium barely divides in humans - cell loss leads to corneal oedema (Fuchs dystrophy).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies the optic cup. From which part of the optic cup does the neural retina develop. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic cup: outer thin layer 4 retinal pigment epithelium; inner thick layer ￿ neural retina; the intraretinal space between them is the site of retinal detachment. Optic stalk 4 optic nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a right-sided oculomotor nerve lesion. Which finding is expected? [BWP 26]

options.C: Right ptosis with impaired eye movements (cannot look up, down or

mcqs.explanation: in) / Exam Pearl: CN111 lesions are ipsilateral (it does not decussate. except fibres to the contralateral SR from the nucleus). Ptosis + mydriasis + down-and-out eye on the same side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces the arterial supply of the orbit. The ophthalmic artery is a branch of which artery. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ophthalmic artery: first branch of ICA after it leaves the cavernous sinus." gives the central retinal artery (end artery - occlusion causes sudden painless blindness with cherry-red spot).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies vessels of the developing eye. Which artery normally regresses during eye development? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The hyaloid artery runs in the choroidal fissure to the lens." its distal part degenerates (remnant: hyaloid canal; persistent 4 floaters, persistent fetal vasculature) while the proximal part becomes the central retinal artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces aqueous humour drainage. After passing through the trabecular meshwork, aqueous humour drains into which structure. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Produced by ciliary epithelium (carbonic anhydrase - acetazolamide reduces it) 4 posterior chamber ￿ pupil 4 anterior chamber 4 trabecular meshwork at the iridocorneal angle 4 canal of Schlemm 4 aqueous veins.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A section shows a vascular pigmented layer between the retina and the f ibrous coat of the eye. Which structure belongs to the same coat as this layer. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The choroid is part of the uvea (vascular tunic) with the ciliary body and iris." sclera and cornea form the fibrous tunic.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Raised intraocular pressure results from obstruction of aqueous outflow. Which site is involved in open-angle glaucoma. [KIMS 26]

options.D: Trabecular meshwork and canal of Schlemm

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Open-angle (chronic, painless, peripheral field loss) - resistance at the trabecular meshwork," closed-angle (acute, painful red eye, halos) - iris blocks the angle; pilocarpine opens it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 6~year-old child has recurrent middle ear infections spreading from the nasopharynx. From which embryological structure does the auditory (Eustachian) tube develop? [Prof 24. CKMC 26. HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 1st pouch ￿ tubotympanic recess (auditory tube, middle ear cavity, mastoid antrum, inner layer of tympanic membrane). 1st cleft 4 external acoustic meatus. 2nd pouch ￿ palatine tonsil.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with chronic otitis media has a cholesteatoma eroding the posterior wall of the middle ear toward the mastoid. Which structure is damaged first? [Prof 24. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The facial canal lies in the medial and posterior walls of the middle ear (above the oval window, then descending behind the cavity) 4 facial palsy in chronic otitis media/mastoid surgery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ENT surgeon studies the membranous labyrinth. Of which structure is the cochlear duct (scala media) a part? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cochlear duct (endolymph) lies between scala vestibuli and scala tympani (perilymph) and carries the organ of Corti on the basilar membrane.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology question asks about the otic vesicle (otocyst). Which structures arise from its ventral (saccular) part? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Otic placode (surface ectoderm) 4 otic vesicle: dorsal utricular part 4 utricle, semicircular ducts. endolymphatic duct; ventral saccular part saccule. cochlear duct (organ of Corti).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient is examined with an otoscope. Of which region of the ear is the external acoustic meatus a part? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: External ear = auricle + external acoustic meatus (lateral 1/3 cartilaginous, medial 2/3 bony,. S-shaped - pull pinna up and back in adults). It develops from the 1st pharyngeal cleft.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has conductive hearing loss from impacted wax. Where is cerumen formed? [Prof 25]

options.D: External auditory canal (cartilaginous part, ceruminous glands)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine sweat glands in the skin of the cartilaginous outer third of the canal; hair and sebaceous glands are also found only there.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with glue ear needs a myringotomy and grommet; the surgeon wants to avoid the chorda tympani and ossicles. In which quadrant of the tympanic membrane should the incision be made. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chorda tympani and the long process of the incus run in the posterosuperior quadrant; myringotomy is done in the posteroinferior (or anteroinferior) quadrant. Cone of light is anteroinferior.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student traces the origin of the inner ear. From which structure is the membranous labyrinth derived? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Otic placode 4 otic pit ￿ otic vesicle 4 entire membranous labyrinth. The bony labyrinth develops from surrounding mesenchyme (otic capsule).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ENT student describes the walls of the middle ear. What forms the lateral wall of the tympanic cavity. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Middle ear." roof - tegmen tympani: floor - jugular bulb,. lateral - tympanic membrane," medial - promontory (basal turn of cochlea). oval and round windows; anterior - carotid canal, auditory tube," posterior - aditus, pyramid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child is born with conductive deafness and malformed ossicles. From which embryological source do the ear ossicles originate. [LHR 25 . QIMS 25]

options.B: Neural crest-derived cartilage of the 1st and 2nd pharyngeal arches

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 1st arch (Meckel cartilage)." malleus, incus. 2nd arch (Reichert cartilage)." stapes (except part of the footplate from otic capsule), styloid process. Arch cartilages are neural crest mesenchyme.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies the tympanic membrane. From which germ layers does it develop. [CKMC 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Outer layer: ectoderm (1st cleft)," middle fibrous layer: mesoderm; inner layer: endoderm (1st pouch). Hence tympanic membrane = all three germ layers.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with otitis media develops a temporal lobe abscess. Which structure forms the roof of the middle ear. [MUL 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tegmen tympani (petrous temporal) separates the middle ear from the middle cranial fossa 4 otogenic temporal lobe abscess and meningitis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During tympanoplasty, a nerve is seen crossing the inner surface of the tympanic membrane. What is the relation of the chorda tympani in the tympanic cavity. [KIMS 26 . WMC 25. HITEC 25]

options.A: It exits through the stylomastoid foramen
options.B: It runs in the pterygoid canal
options.C: It lies in the internal acoustic meatus
options.D: It runs on the medial surface of the tympanic membrane between

mcqs.explanation: the handle of malleus and long process of incus / Exam Pearl: Chorda tympani leaves the facial canal-6 mm above the stylomastoid foramen. enters via the posterior canaliculus, crosses the TM. exits through the petrotympanic fissure and joins the lingual nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with chronic otitis media develops septic thrombosis of the internal jugular vein. Through which wall/route does infection reach the jugular bulb? [BWP 25]

options.A: Floor of the middle ear (jugular bulb/jugular foramen)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Floor of the tympanic cavity is a thin plate over the jugular bulb; infection may cause lateral sinus/lJV thrombophlebitis. Anterior wall." carotid canal; roof: tegmen tympani.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient f inds normal sounds painfully loud after a facial nerve lesion. Which nerve supplies the stapedius. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stapedius (2nd arch. Vll) dampens stapes movement," tensor tympani (1st arch, V3) tenses the drum. Stapedius palsy 4 hyperacusis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has malformed, low-set external ears. Which embryological structures form the auricle? [KIMS 25]

options.D: Six auricular hillocks of the 1st and 2nd pharyngeal arches

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Auricle develops from three hillocks on each of the 1st and 2nd arches around the 1st cleft; ears ascend from the neck to the side of the head. Low-set ears suggest chromosomal syndromes (trisomy 18, 13. 21).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies cochlear development. From which structure does the organ of Corti develop. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The cochlear duct grows out of the saccular part of the otic vesicle; its epithelium differentiates into the organ of Corti (hair cells. supporting cells), covered by the tectorial membrane.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon notes that a middle ear infection may spread to a major artery. Which structure is related to the anterior wall of the middle ear. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior wall.. thin plate over the carotid canal, opening of the auditory tube and canal for tensor tympani. Floor: jugular bulb. Posterior: aditus to antrum, pyramid, facial canal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has hearing loss and vertigo from a cerebellopontine angle tumour. Which cranial nerve is responsible for hearing and equilibrium. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN Vlll leaves through the internal acoustic meatus with Vll," vestibular schwannoma presents with unilateral SNHL, tinnitus and imbalance, later facial numbness (V) and weakness (Vll).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 5-year-old has severe ear pain from acute otitis media. Which cranial nerve carries pain from the medial surface of the tympanic membrane and middle ear. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tympanic membrane: outer surface - auriculotemporal (V3) and auricular branch of X (Arnold nerve; cough on ear cleaning)," inner surface and middle ear - tympanic nerve of IX. Referred otalgia from tonsils/pharynx via IX and X.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student lists derivatives of the pharyngeal arches. Which is a derivative of the second arch? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arch 2 (Reichert cartilage)." stapes, styloid process, stylohyoid ligament, lesser horn and upper body of hyoid. Arch I: malleus, incus, Meckel cartilage. sphenomandibular ligament; tensor tympani (V3).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student lists the muscles of the middle ear. Which nerve supplies the tensor tympani. [KIMS 26]

options.A: Trigeminal nerve (V3, nerve to medial pterygoid)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini are Ist-arch muscles (V3)," stapedius is 2nd-arch (Vll).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: During tonsillectomy, the surgeon dissects the tonsillar bed. Which muscle forms the lateral wall (bed) of the tonsillar fossa. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Tonsil bed." pharyngobasilar fascia + superior constrictor (+ styloglossus); beyond lie the glossopharyngeal nerve. facial artery loop and parapharyngeal space. Bleeding is commonly from the external palatine (paratonsillar) vein.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A newborn has a depressed soft palate and the uvula deviates to one side because the vagal supply to the palate is def icient. Which pharyngeal arch is involved? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: I: Arch nerves: l 4 V3, 2 ￿ Vll, 3 ￿ IX (stylopharyngeus), 4 ￿ X superior laryngeal (cricothyroid, constrictors, levator palati), 6 ￿ recurrent laryngeal (intrinsic laryngeal muscles).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A histologist examines the tongue and finds serous glands opening into troughs around large papillae. Into which papillae do von Ebner glands open. [Prof 24. LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Circumvallate papillae (8- 12. in front of sulcus terminalis) have taste buds in their walls." von Ebner serous glands flush the trench. Filiform papillae have no taste buds.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a lesion of the posterior third of the tongue loses both general sensation and taste there. Which nerve supplies this area. [Prof 24 . Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: I: Anterior 2/3." general sensation V3 (lingual), taste Vll (chorda tympani). Posterior 1/3 (incl. circumvallate papillae): both by IX. Root of tongue near epiglottis: internal laryngeal (X). Motor." Xll except palatoglossus (X).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A histology lecture describes taste papillae arranged in a V. Where are the circumvallate papillae located? [Prof 25. LHR 25 . BWP 25]

options.C: Immediately in front of the sulcus terminalis
options.D: Lateral edge of the tongue only

mcqs.explanation: Circumvallate papillae lie in a V just anterior to the sulcus terminalis (developmentally part of the anterior 2/3) but are supplied by IX. Foliate papillae are on the lateral margins.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A newborn has a short lingual frenulum and cannot latch properly to feed. Which function is mainly affected in ankyloglossia. [Prof 25. CKMC 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: I: Ankyloglossia (tongue-tie): short frenulum restricts protrusion and elevation 4 feeding and speech problems; treated by frenotomy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A diabetic has a brawny swelling of the floor of the mouth, an elevated tongue and stridor after a lower molar infection. Which spaces are involved in Ludwig angina. [Prof 25 . CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Ludwig angina: bilateral cellulitis of submandibular, sublingual and submental spaces (2nd/3rd molar roots lie below mylohyoid line) 4 airway obstruction; spread to parapharyngeal space and mediastinum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A child with chronic mouth breathing and snoring has enlarged tonsils in the roof of the nasopharynx. What is the tonsil of the nasopharynx called? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Waldeyer ring: pharyngeal (adenoid, roof/posterior wall of nasopharynx), tubal (around auditory tube opening), palatine and lingual tonsils. Enlarged adenoids ￿ adenoid facies, otitis media with effusion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A man feels a fish bone stuck in his throat on one side of the larynx. Where does a fish bone usually lodge. [LHR 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Piriform fossa lies lateral to the aryepiglottic fold; the internal laryngeal nerve runs under its mucosa and may be injured during removal (loss of cough reflex). Tonsils and vallecula are other sites.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A dentist explains how taste from the anterior tongue reaches the brain. Taste fibres from the anterior two-thirds travel first with which nerve. [CKMC 25]
