mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Taste fibres run in the lingual nerve, leave it as the chorda tympani, reach the geniculate ganglion (cell bodies) and end in the nucleus of the tractus solitarius.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A newborn has mandibular hypoplasia, downward-slanting palpebral fissures, malformed external ears and conductive deafness. Abnormal development of which arch causes Treacher Collins syndrome. [CKMC 25. MUL 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: First arch syndromes (Treacher Collins - TCOFI, neural crest.. Pierre Robin) affect mandible, maxilla, malleus. incus, external ear and muscles of mastication.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A newborn has micrognathia, cleft palate and airway obstruction because the tongue falls backwards. What is this condition. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Robin sequence: mandibular hypoplasia 4 posterior displacement of the tongue (glossoptosis) ￿ prevents palatal shelf fusion 4 U-shaped cleft palate and airway obstruction," prone positioning helps.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: During dissection of the submandibular region, the student traces the lingual artery. What is its relation to the hyoglossus muscle. [CKMC 25. HITEC 25]

options.A: It passes deep (medial) to hyoglossus, while the hypoglossal nerve
options.B: It pierces the hyoglossus lies superficial
options.C: It runs superficial to hyoglossus with the lingual nerve
options.D: It lies posterior to the muscle only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial to hyoglossus: lingual nerve, submandibular ganglion, submandibular duct, hypoglossal nerve. Deep to it: lingual artery, glossopharyngeal nerve, stylohyoid ligament. Key note: source said "over" the hyoglossus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient with dermatomyositis has dysphagia from weakness of the upper oesophagus. What type of muscle is in the upper third of the oesophagus? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Upper third: skeletal; middle third: mixed.. lower third: smooth. Skeletal muscle diseases (myasthenia, dermatomyositis) affect the upper oesophagus; achalasia and systemic sclerosis affect the lower.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient bleeds briskly from the tonsillar bed after tonsillectomy. Which artery is the main arterial supply of the palatine tonsil? [MUL 25]

options.D: Tonsillar branch of the facial artery

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tonsillar artery (facial) pierces the superior constrictor; others: ascending palatine, dorsal lingual, ascending pharyngeal. descending palatine. Post-tonsillectomy bleeding is often venous (external palatine/paratonsillar vein).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient cannot draw his tongue backward and upward during swallowing. Which muscle retracts the tongue. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Genioglossus protrudes." hyoglossus depresses; styloglossus retracts and elevates: palatoglossus (X) elevates the root. All except palatoglossus supplied by Xll.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A slide of the tongue dorsum shows numerous slender keratinized papillae without taste buds. Which papillae are these. [KIMS 26 . MUL 25. BWP 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Filiform: most numerous, keratinized, no taste buds, give rough texture. Fungiform." mushroom-shaped, red, scattered, taste buds on top. Circumvallate." 8-12, taste buds in walls.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: After an inferior alveolar block, a patient's anterior tongue feels numb. Which nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue? [HITEC 26. MUL 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lingual nerve (V3) lies close to the inferior alveolar nerve and is often anaesthetized with it; at the third molar it lies just below the mucosa against the lingual plate.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: After adenoidectomy, a child has numbness of the nasopharyngeal mucosa. Which nerve supplies sensation to the nasopharynx (around the adenoids)? [MUL 25]

options.A: Glossopharyngeal nerve (pharyngeal plexus) with pharyngeal branch

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Nasopharynx." mainly pharyngeal branch of the pterygopalatine ganglion (V2) and IX; oropharynx: IX; laryngopharynx: X (internal laryngeal). Pain after adenoidectomy may refer to the ear (IX).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A student asks why the vermilion border of the lips is red. What explains its red colour. [AMC 26 . HITEC 26. HITEC 25]

options.C: Thin epithelium, little melanin and a rich capillary supply in tall

mcqs.explanation: dermal papillae / Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Vermilion (red) zone: thin, lightly keratinized epithelium, high dermal papillae with capillaries close to the surface, little pigment, no hair, sweat or sebaceous glands ￿ needs saliva to stay moist.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: During tonsillectomy, the surgeon encounters the main source of troublesome bleeding. Which vessel is it? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. External palatine vein descends from the soft palate on the lateral surface of the tonsil to the pharyngeal plexus - the commonest cause of post-tonsillectomy bleeding.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A picture of the developing tongue is shown. From which pharyngeal arch is the posterior one-third of the tongue mainly derived? [HITEC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior 2/3.. 1st arch (lateral lingual swellings + tuberculum impar) - V3 sensory. Posterior 1/3: 3rd arch (hypobranchial eminence/copula overgrowing the 2nd) - IX. Posterior-most part/epiglottis: 4th arch - X. Muscles: occipital myotomes - Xll.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A diagram of tongue development labels A (lateral lingual swellings) and B (tuberculum impar). Which structures mainly form the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. [HITEC 25]

options.B: Lateral lingual swellings of the 1st arch

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Two lateral lingual swellings overgrow the median tuberculum impar to form most of the anterior 2/3," the sulcus terminalis marks the junction with the posterior third.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A student asks which nerve supplies the most posterior part of the tongue near the epiglottis. From which arch and nerve is it derived? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. The posterior-most part of the tongue and the epiglottic region come from the 4th arch supplied by the internal laryngeal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (X).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient has a lower motor neuron lesion of the left hypoglossal nerve. To which side does the tongue deviate on protrusion? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. The intact genioglossus pushes the tongue toward the paralysed side ("lick your wounds")," LMN lesions also cause wasting and fasciculation. Uvula. in contrast, deviates to the NORMAL side in vagal palsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A student asks which muscle elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing and is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve. Which muscle is it? [HITEC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stylopharyngeus - only muscle of the 3rd arch (IX); passes between superior and middle constrictors to insert on the thyroid cartilage near the piriform recess. Source stem ("closure of piriform recess") was unclear; reconstructed.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient with a peritonsillar abscess develops spread into the parapharyngeal space. Which muscle must the infection breach? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The tonsillar bed (superior constrictor + pharyngobasilar fascia) separates the peritonsillar space from the parapharyngeal space.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: An elderly man regurgitates undigested food and has a neck swelling; barium swallow shows a pouch. Through which weak area does a Zenker diverticulum herniate. [BWP 25]

options.C: Killian dehiscence between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus

mcqs.explanation: (inferior constrictor) / Exam Pearl: Pharyngeal pouch." pulsion diverticulum through Killian dehiscence posteriorly. due to cricopharyngeal dysfunction; appears usually on the left. Source mentioned "after thyroid surgery"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A man cannot protrude his tongue properly; it deviates to the right on protrusion. Which muscle is paralysed? [QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Genioglossus (Xll) is the main protruder: each pulls the tongue forward and to the opposite side. so a weak right genioglossus lets the tongue deviate to the right.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A 2-day-old infant has difficulty swallowing and a large tongue protruding from the mouth. What is this condition. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Macroglossia." congenital hypothyroidism (cretinism), Down syndrome, Beckwith-wiedemann syndrome, lymphangioma. amyloidosis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A man loses taste on the anterior tongue. Which papillae there carry most taste buds. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Fungiform papillae (anterior 2/3, chorda tympani) have taste buds on their upper surface," filiform papillae have none,. circumvallate (IX) are in front of the sulcus terminalis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: After thyroid surgery, a man has difficulty swallowing. Injury to which nerve supplying the pharyngeal constrictors is suspected? [KIMS 25]

options.A: Vagus (CN X) via the pharyngeal plexus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. All pharyngeal muscles are supplied by X (pharyngeal plexus) except stylopharyngeus (IX). The inferior constrictor also receives external and recurrent laryngeal branches.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A doctor gives sublingual nitroglycerin, which is absorbed through a visible vein under the tongue. Which vein is visible on the inferior surface of the tongue. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep lingual veins lie on either side of the frenulum beneath thin mucosa (lingual nerve lateral to them) - the basis of rapid sublingual drug absorption.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A patient with a unilateral vagus nerve lesion is asked to say ah" In which direction does the uvula deviate. [AMC 26]

options.A: Away from the paralysed side (toward the normal side)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intact levator veli palatini pulls the palate and uvula toward the healthy side," the affected palatal arch sags. Contrast: tongue deviates TOWARD a paralysed hypoglossal side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: During excision of the submandibular gland, the surgeon must protect a nerve that loops around the duct. What is the relationship of the lingual nerve to the submandibular duct? [AMC 26. HITEC 26]

options.C: It passes lateral then inferior to the duct and crosses to its medial

mcqs.explanation: side J Exam Pearl: The lingual nerve "double-crosses" the submandibular duct: first lateral, then below it. then medial - on the hyoglossus. The hypoglossal nerve lies below the duct.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A surgeon examines the upper pharyngeal wall above the superior constrictor. Which fascia is attached to the skull base and fills the gap above the superior constrictor. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pharyngobasilar fascia (thickened submucosa) attaches to the basiocciput and petrous temporal; the auditory tube and levator veli palatini pass through the gap above the superior constrictor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A man has epigastric pain relieved by eating that recurs 2-3 hours later and wakes him at night. What is the most likely diagnosis. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Duodenal ulcer: pain relieved by food/antacids, recurs when the stomach empties (2-3 h) and at night; associated with H. pylori and acid hypersecretion. Gastric ulcer pain is worsened by food.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: The posterior part of the anterior tongue shows a V-shaped row of large, flat-topped papillae. Which papillae are these. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Circumvallate papillae: 8-12 large flat-topped papillae each surrounded by a trench, in front of the sulcus terminalis; taste buds on their side walls; supplied by IX.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A newborn has a cleft in the anterior part of the tongue because two midline structures failed to fuse. What is this anomaly. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Bifid (cleft) tongue failure of fusion of the lateral lingual swellings

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the original referred to a figure. Incomplete fvsion of the lateral lingual swellings produces a bifid tongue." ankyloglossia is a short frenulum; macroglossia an enlarged tongue.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A fish bone lodges in the piriform recess. Of which region is the piriform recess a part? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Laryngopharynx extends from the epiglottis to the lower border of cricoid (C6) and contains the piriform recesses on either side of the laryngeal inlet.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: A child with recurrent throat infections has enlarged lymphoid tissue around the pharyngeal openings. Which combination forms Waldeyer ring. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Palatine, lingual and the palatine arches
options.C: Lingual, palatine, pharyngeal and tubal tonsils
options.D: Lingual, tubal, palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal tonsils

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Waldeyer ring guards the entrance to the aerodigestive tract." pharyngeal (adenoid), tubal, palatine and lingual tonsils with scattered lymphoid nodules; palatine tonsil is the largest.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Oral Cavity, Lips, Tongue, Pharynx & Esophagus
mcqs.question: During tongue development, a midline swelling from the second arch is overgrown by the hypobranchial eminence. What is this swelling called? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Copula (2nd arch) is overgrown by the hypobranchial eminence (3rd and 4th arches) - so the 2nd arch contributes no sensory supply to the adult tongue (no Vll general sensation).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a head injury, a man has clear watery nasal discharge that tests positive for glucose and P2-transferrin. Which bone is fractured? [Prof 24. CKMC 26. CKMC 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cribriform plate fracture tears the meninges around olfactory nerve filaments 4 CSF rhinorrhoea, anosmia, risk of meningitis. F2-transferrin is specific for CSF.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient is hoarse after thyroid surgery. The recurrent laryngeal nerve is a branch of which nerve? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Right RLN hooks under the subclavian artery, left under the arch of aorta (longer, more often injured); supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid; posterior cricoarytenoid is the only abductor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with severe posterior epistaxis needs ligation of the main artery of the nasal cavity. Which artery, a branch of the maxillary artery, is ligated? [Prof 25 . AMC 26 . CKMC 26 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sphenopalatine artery ("artery of epistaxis") enters via the sphenopalatine foramen; posterior bleeds need posterior packing or endoscopic ligation. Anterior bleeds arise from Kiesselbach/Little area.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An endoscopic sinus surgeon examines the medial wall of the maxillary sinus. Which structure opens through the medial wall of the maxillary sinus. [AMC 25]

options.B: The sinus ostium into the hiatus semilunaris (middle meatus)
options.C: The nasolacrimal duct into the sinus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Maxillary ostium lies high on the medial wall ￿ poor gravity drainage; floor is related to roots of upper molars/premolars; roof is the orbital floor with the infraorbital nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boy is hit on the nose and bleeds from the front of the nasal septum. Which structure is most likely damaged? [HITEC 26. AMC 25. HITEC 25]

options.A: Kiesselbach plexus (Little area) on the anterior septum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Kiesselbach plexus: anterior ethmoidal, septal branch of sphenopalatine, greater the site of -90% of nosebleeds. palatine and superior labial (facial) arteries

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman becomes hoarse after thyroidectomy. Damage to which nerve is responsible. [AMC 25. LHR 25. HITEC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RLN runs in the tracheo-oesophageal groove close to the inferior thyroid artery; unilateral injury 4 hoarseness (paramedian cord); bilateral stridor. External laryngeal injury 4 weak high-pitched voice (cricothyroid).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A singer cannot reach high notes after thyroid surgery; laryngoscopy shows a lax vocal cord. Which nerve supplies the cricothyroid muscle? [AMC 26. LHR 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid cartilage forward 4 tenses and lengthens the vocal cords (pitch). External laryngeal nerve (from superior laryngeal, X) runs with the superior thyroid artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A baby has a watery eye because the nasolacrimal duct has not canalized. Where does the nasolacrimal duct open. [BWP 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior meatus: nasolacrimal duct. Middle meatus: frontal, maxillary, anterior and middle ethmoidal sinuses. Superior meatus: posterior ethmoidal. Sphenoethmoidal recess: sphenoid sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child inhales a peanut that lodges at the narrowest part of the laryngeal cavity. What is the narrowest part of the adult laryngeal cavity. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Adults: rima glottidis (between vocal folds); infants." subglottic region at the cricoid ring (complete ring, cannot expand).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with epiglottitis has a swollen structure at the laryngeal inlet. Which cartilage forms the main (anterior) boundary of the laryngeal inlet? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Laryngeal inlet." epiglottis (anterior), aryepiglottic folds (lateral), interarytenoid fold (posterior). Epiglottis is elastic cartilage and does not ossify.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During clinical examination, the maxillary sinus is transilluminated. From where is the light shone. [WMC 25]

options.B: Inside the mouth (against the hard palate/roof of mouth)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Maxillary sinus: light in the mouth with lips closed." frontal sinus." light under the medial supraorbital margin. A fluid-filled sinus appears dark.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has frontal headache that worsens on bending forward, with tenderness above the medial eyebrow. Which sinus is infected? [HfrEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sinus pain: frontal 4 forehead (supraorbital, supratrochlear nerves)." ethmoid 4 between the eyes/medial canthus (nasociliary)." sphenoid 4 vertex, deep retro-orbital: maxillary 4 cheek. upper teeth. Frontal sinus drains via the frontonasal duct into the hiatus semilunaris.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has pain between the eyes and at the medial canthus with nasal discharge. Infection of which sinus is most likely, and which nerve carries the pain? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Ethmoid air cells are supplied by anterior and posterior ethmoidal branches of the nasociliary nerve (Vl); posterior ethmoidal also supplies the sphenoid sinus (vertex/retro-orbital pain).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with frontal sinusitis has fluid in the frontal sinus on imaging. Through which structure does the frontal sinus drain into the nasal cavity. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Hiatus semilunaris (via the frontonasal duct, middle meatus)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoidal sinuses open into the hiatus semilunaris (ostiomeatal complex)," middle ethmoidal cells open on the bulla.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After extraction of an upper third molar, the root is displaced into the maxillary sinus and pus drains into the nose. Into which meatus does the maxillary sinus drain. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Maxillary ostium opens into the hiatus semilunaris of the middle meatus. Upper molar and premolar roots project into the sinus floor ￿ oroantral fistula after extraction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boxer is struck on the nose and bleeds from the anterior part of the nasal septum. Which artery contributes to the anterior septal (Kiesselbach) plexus from above? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Kiesselbach plexus = anterior ethmoidal + sphenopalatine (septal) + greater palatine + superior labial arteries. The anterior ethmoidal enters the nose from above near the front of the septum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In a car crash, a man's neck is struck by the seat belt; he has a sore Adam's apple and difficulty breathing. Which cartilage is most likely fractured? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. The laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple) is formed by the thyroid laminae meeting at 90° in males; thyroid cartilage ossifies with age and fractures with blunt trauma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A fish bone scratches the mucosa of the laryngeal inlet and the patient has no cough reflex. Which nerve supplies sensation to the larynx above the vocal folds. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Above the vocal folds: internal laryngeal (sensory, pierces thyrohyoid membrane. under piriform fossa mucosa),. below the folds: recurrent laryngeal. Internal laryngeal nerve damage ￿ aspiration.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After thyroid surgery a patient is hoarse; laryngoscopy shows one vocal cord fixed near the midline. Which nerve was injured? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Unilateral RLN palsy: cord in paramedian position (cricothyroid still adducts), hoarse/breathy voice; the opposite cord compensates over time. Bilateral palsy 4 stridor needing tracheostomy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student asks about laryngeal muscle innervation. Which nerve supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RLN also supplies sensation below the vocal folds and the inferior constrictor (cricopharyngeus). Posterior cricoarytenoid ("safety muscle") is the only abductor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A fetus has respiratory distress because the muscle that opens the rima glottidis failed to form. Which muscle is it? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior cricoarytenoid - the only abductor (rotates arytenoids laterally). Adductors: lateral cricoarytenoid, transverse/oblique arytenoids, thyroarytenoid. Tensor: cricothyroid. Relaxer: thyroarytenoid/vocalis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A baby has a tuft of excess hair over the lower back. What is excessive hair growth that develops from abnormal hair follicle formation called? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Hypertrichosis: excess hair from overabundance of follicles (may be localized, e.g. over spina bifida occulta). Hirsutism = androgen-driven male-pattern hair in women.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A young woman has depigmented, sharply demarcated white patches on her hands and face. Loss of which cells due to autoimmune destruction causes vitiligo. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Melanocytes (neural crest) lie in the stratum basale and transfer melanosomes to keratinocytes; vitiligo is autoimmune melanocyte loss (associated with thyroid disease, type l DM, Addison).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies development of skin appendages. From which germ layer are sweat glands derived? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Epidermis and its appendages (hair, nails, sweat, sebaceous and mammary glands) are surface ectoderm: dermis is mesoderm; melanocytes are neural crest.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide shows a tube lined by tall cells with long non-motile apical processes, storing sperm. What epithelium lines the epididymis. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Stereocilia are long microvilli (absorptive) found in epididymis, vas deferens and inner ear hair cells. Respiratory epithelium has motile cilia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with callus formation has thickened skin of the palms. Increased activity of which cells causes skin thickening. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Keratinocytes (~ 90% of epidermal cells) proliferate in the stratum basale and keratinize," friction causes hyperkeratosis. Langerhans cells are antigen-presenting; Merkel cells are mechanoreceptors.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 12-year-old boy has a painless midline neck swelling that moves up on protruding the tongue. What is the diagnosis. [Prof 24. AMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroglossal cyst: remnant of the thyroglossal duct (foramen caecum 4 thyroid), midline, usually infrahyoid, moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion; Sistrunk operation removes the middle of the hyoid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist studies a craniopharyngioma arising from remnants of Rathke pouch. From which structure does Rathke pouch arise? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) from Rathke pouch - ectodermal outgrowth of the stomodeum roof; posterior pituitary from the infundibulum (neuroectoderm, diencephalon). Craniopharyngioma calcifies, compresses the chiasma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During thyroidectomy, the surgeon ligates the artery supplying the lower pole of the thyroid. From which artery does it arise. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior thyroid artery (first branch of ECA) - ligate close to the gland to save the external laryngeal nerve; inferior thyroid artery (thyrocervical trunk) - ligate away from the gland to save the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon removing the thyroid tries to preserve the parathyroid glands. Where are they normally located? [Prof 25]

options.B: On the posterior border of the lateral lobes

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior parathyroids (4th pouch) are constant near the middle of the posterior border; inferior parathyroids (3rd pouch, descend with thymus) are variable, near the lower pole and inferior thyroid artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist examines a parathyroid adenoma causing hypercalcaemia. Which cells secrete parathyroid hormone. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chief cells." small. numerous, secrete PTH. Oxyphil cells: larger, eosinophilic (many mitochondria), appear after puberty. function uncertain. C cells (thyroid) secrete calcitonin.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has a neuroblastoma arising from the adrenal medulla. From which germ layer is the adrenal medulla derived? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Adrenal cortex = mesoderm (coelomic epithelium); medulla = neural crest (chromaffin cells, modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons). Neuroblastoma and phaeochromocytoma arise from neural crest.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During thyroidectomy, the surgeon ligates both thyroid arteries. Which nerves are at risk with the superior and inferior thyroid arteries respectively. [KIMS 26 . CKMC 25 . KIMS 25]

options.B: External laryngeal nerve; recurrent laryngeal nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created. the source recalled only the stem and answer. Ligate superior thyroid artery close to the upper pole (external laryngeal nerve diverges away); ligate inferior thyroid artery well lateral (RLN crosses its branches near the gland).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student identifies the pit at the apex of the sulcus terminalis. Which organ develops from the foramen caecum. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid diverticulum arises at the foramen caecum (between tuberculum impar and copula) and descends via the thyroglossal duct; ectopic lingual thyroid may be the only thyroid tissue.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist stains anterior pituitary cells. Somatotrophs (GH-secreting cells) belong to which staining group. [KIMS 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Acidophils: somatotrophs (GH) and lactotrophs (PRL). Basophils: corticotrophs (ACTH), thyrotrophs (TSH), gonadotrophs (FSH, LH) - B~FLAT" Pituicytes are glia of the posterior lobe.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A thyroid biopsy from a woman with Graves disease shows small follicles with scalloped colloid. What happens to follicular cells in hyperthyroidism. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Active follicles: tall columnar cells, scant scalloped colloid (resorption vacuoles). Inactive (hypothyroid, colloid goitre): flat cuboidal/squamous cells with abundant colloid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has hypocalcaemic tetany, recurrent infections, a conotruncal heart defect and abnormal facies. Which syndrome is this. [CKMC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DiGeorge." failure of 3rd and 4th pouches ￿ absent thymus (T-cell deficiency) and parathyroids (hypocalcaemia) + cardiac outflow and facial anomalies ("CATCH-22").

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During thyroidectomy, the surgeon ligates the middle thyroid vein. Into which vein does it drain. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Superior and middle thyroid veins 4 IJV," inferior thyroid veins 4 left brachiocephalic vein. The middle thyroid vein is short and must be ligated first to mobilize the lobe.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroendocrinology student traces the blood supply of the pituitary. What do the superior hypophyseal arteries primarily supply. [AMC 26]

options.B: The median eminencefinfundibulum, forming the hypophyseal portal system to the anterior lobe

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior hypophyseal arteries (ICA) 4 primary capillary plexus in the median eminence 4 portal veins ￿ secondary plexus in the anterior lobe (carrying releasing hormones). Inferior hypophyseal arteries 4 posterior lobe.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During total thyroidectomy, the surgeon ligates the vessels at the upper pole. Which vessel is closely related to the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. [LHR 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: External laryngeal nerve runs with the superior thyroid artery toward the cricothyroid; ligate the artery close to the gland ("Joll space"). Injury weak, monotonous voice, inability to reach high notes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon performing a tracheostomy must divide or retract the thyroid isthmus. The thyroid isthmus usually lies anterior to which tracheal rings. [LHR 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isthmus covers tracheal rings 2~4,. lateral lobes extend from the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage to the 6th tracheal ring. A pyramidal lobe may ascend from the isthmus (thyroglossal duct remnant).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist identifies the cell of origin of a GH-secreting adenoma. Which pituitary cells secrete growth hormone? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Somatotrophs are the most numerous anterior pituitary cells (-50¥), acidophilic, located mainly in the lateral wings; adenomas cause gigantism/acromegaly.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A CT scan shows a swelling extending behind the trachea in the lower neck. From which gland does a retrotracheal swelling most likely arise. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A large multinodular goitre may extend posteriorly behind the trachea/oesophagus or retrosternally, compressing the airway (Pemberton sign).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student asks which adrenal cells make steroid hormones. Which cells produce steroid hormones. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Steroid-secreting cells (adrenal cortex, Leydig, corpus luteum) have abundant SER, lipid droplets and mitochondria with tubular cristae. Chromaffin cells secrete catecholamines.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student labels the adrenal cortex. Which zone secretes aldosterone. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Zona glomerulosa: outer, arched clusters, mineralocorticoids (aldosterone synthase). It is NOT atrophied by exogenous steroids because it is controlled by angiotensin11 and K..

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman with an adrenal tumour has virilization. Which zone secretes adrenal androgens. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Zona reticularis (innermost, anastomosing cords, lipofuscin) makes DHEA, DHEA-S and androstenedione (under ACTH); adrenarche begins -age 6-8.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student matches pharyngeal structures with their derivatives. Which pairing is correct? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Third pharyngeal pouch - inferior parathyroid glands (and thymus)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pouches: l ￿ middle ear/auditory tube," 2 4 palatine tonsil; 3 ￿ inferior parathyroids + thymus," 4 4 superior parathyroids + ultimobranchial body (C cells). Laryngeal cartilages: arches 4 and 6.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man on prolonged high-dose prednisolone develops adrenal suppression. Which zone of the adrenal cortex atrophies most? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Exogenous glucocorticoids suppress CRH/ACTH 4 atrophy of ACTH-dependent zones (fasciculata, reticularis): glomerulosa is preserved (renin-angiotensin). Abrupt withdrawal 4 adrenal crisis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student is asked where light energy is converted to electrical signals in the eye. In which cells does phototransduction occur? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created: the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Photopigments (rhodopsin, cone opsins) in outer-segment discs absorb light 4 transducin PDE 4 I CGMP ￿ closure of Na, channels 4 hyperpolarization. Ganglion cells are the first to fire action potentials.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old man has to hold his newspaper at arm's length to read. What causes presbyopia. [HITEC 26. AMC 25. QIMS 25]

options.B: Loss of elasticity of the lens

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: With age the lens becomes stiff and accommodation falls (near point recedes); by-70 years the lens is almost non-accommodating. Correct with convex (plus) lenses for near work.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man cannot distinguish red from green on stained histology slides. Which cells are defective. [AMC 25 . KIMS 25]

options.A: Cones (a red or green cone opsin)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Red-green colour blindness is X-linked recessive (opsin genes on Xq28,. _8% of males): protanopia = red cones absent, deuteranopia = green cones absent. Tested with Ishihara plates.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with neurosyphilis has small pupils that constrict to near objects but not to light. Damage at which site causes this. [LHR 25]

options.B: Pretectal nucleus (light-reflex pathway in the dorsal midbrain)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Argyll Robertson pupil: lesion of pretectal 4 EW fibres (light reflex) sparing the more ventral accommodation pathway. Adie pupil: ciliary ganglion lesion (tonic, dilated pupil).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with vitamin A def iciency has night blindness. Which cells are primarily affected? [QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rhodopsin = opsin + 11-cis-retinal (vitamin A aldehyde). Deficiency 4 slow dark adaptation, nyctalopia. xerophthalmia. Bitot spots. keratomalacia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old girl has a pituitary tumour removed and is left blind in the temporal fields of both eyes. Which structure is affected? [CKMC 26. KIMS 26. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bitemporal (heteronymous) hemianopia = crossing nasal fibres in the chiasma. Optic tract ￿ contralateral homonymous hemianopia; Meyer loop superior quadrantanopia ("pie in the sky").

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man sees vertical lines clearly but horizontal lines blurred. What is the defect in astigmatism? [QIMS 25]

options.B: Unequal curvature of the cornea (or lens) in different meridians
options.C: Light focused in front of the retina

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Astigmatism: refractive power differs in two planes ￿ point focus impossible; corrected with cylindrical lenses. Key note: none of the source options was correct (they described hyperopia, myopia, emmetropia and cataract).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: When light hits a rod photoreceptor, the cell hyperpolarizes. Which event causes this. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]

options.C: Increase in K, conductance into the outer segment
options.D: Decrease in Na, conductance in the outer segment (closure of

mcqs.explanation: cGMP-gated channels) / Exam Pearl: Dark: cGMP-gated Na, channels open (dark current. -40 mv) ￿ glutamate release. Light: rhodopsin 4 transducin 4 PDE6 4 I CGMP 4 channels close ￿ hyperpolarization (-70 mv) ￿ less glutamate.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The nasal visual field of the right eye falls on the temporal retina of the right eye. To which optic tract do these fibres project? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Temporal retinal fibres (nasal field) do not cross and run in the ipsilateral tract; nasal retinal fibres (temporal field) cross in the chiasma. Each tract therefore carries the contralateral visual field.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with uncorrected myopia has blurred distance vision. What is the usual cause. [KIMS 25]

options.D: Elongated eyeball so that images form in front of the retina

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Myopia: long eye or too strong refraction 4 focus in front of retina." corrected with concave (minus) lenses. Hyperopia: short eye ￿ convex lenses.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old emmetropic man finds near work difficult. What happens to the near point in presbyopia. [AMC 26]

options.A: The far point moves farther away
options.C: The near point moves farther away

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Near point recedes from -9 cm at age 10 to ~25 cm at 40 and- I m at 60 as accommodation (amplitude in dioptres) falls. The far point of an emmetrope stays at infinity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Light shone into the left eye produces no constriction of either pupil, but light in the right eye constricts both. Where is the lesion. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Afferent defect: neither pupil reacts to light in the affected eye but both react from the normal eye (relative afferent pupillary defect, swinging flashlight test). Efferent (111) lesion: affected pupil never constricts.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pathologist cannot see red stains because of red colour blindness. What is this condition called? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prot- _ red (1st), deuter- green (2nd), trit- = blue (3rd); _anopia = absent cone type. -anomaly = abnormal pigment. Achromatopsia = complete colour blindness (rod monochromacy).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks how the retina enhances contrast at edges. Lateral inhibition in the retina is primarily mediated by which cells? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Horizontal cells (outer plexiform layer) inhibit neighbouring photoreceptor-bipolar synapses 4 centre-surround receptive fields and contrast enhancement. Amacrine cells do so in the inner plexiform layer.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man takes several minutes to see in a dark cinema. Which photoreceptors function in dim light? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rods: scotopic (night) vision, high sensitivity, low acuity (many rods converge on one ganglion cell), absent from the fovea; cones: photopic, colour, high acuity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student looks from a distant tree to a book in her hand. Which muscle contracts in the accommodation reflex. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Accommodation triad: ciliary muscle contraction (lens becomes rounder), pupillary constriction (sphincter pupillae), convergence (medial recti) - all via CN111 (parasympathetic. EW).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist traces the visual pathway. Which structure relays visual signals to the visual cortex. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LGN (6 layers: magno 1-2, parvo 3-6." ipsilateral eye 2, 3, 5) 4 optic radiation 4 area 17. MGN relays hearing; VPM relays taste and face sensation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old has a gradual loss of peripheral vision and cupping of the optic disc. Glaucoma is classically characterized by what? [CKMC 26]

options.B: Raised intraocular pressure damaging the optic nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aqueous humour." ciliary processes 4 posterior chamber 4 pupil ￿ anterior chamber ￿ trabecular meshwork ￿ canal of Schlemm. Obstruction raises IOP (>21 mmHg) 4 optic disc cupping, field loss.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist records from rods kept in darkness. What does the high CGMP in photoreceptors in darkness cause. [CKMC 26]

options.C: Increased dark current (Na. influx) and depolarization

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In darkness CGMP keeps cation channels open 4 steady inward dark current" 4 membrane~-40 mv ￿ continuous glutamate release onto bipolar cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student lists photopigments. Which visual pigment is present in rods. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rhodopsin (scotopsin + I l-cis-retinal) absorbs maximally at~505 nm; cone photopsins (iodopsins) peak at-445 (blue), 535 (green) and 570 nm (red); melanopsin in intrinsically photosensitive ganglion cells (circadian, pupil).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist traces the light cascade in rods. Which G-protein activates CGMP phosphodiesterase. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Activated rhodopsin (metarhodopsin11) activates hundreds of transducin molecules 4 PDE6 4 CGMP hydrolysis - huge amplification allowing detection of single photons.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient cannot see the left temporal visual field or the right nasal visual field. Where is the lesion (as keyed in the source)? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of left temporal + right nasal field = left homonymous hemianopia 4 RIGHT optic tract (or radiation). Key note." source keyed optic chiasma; the pattern described is homonymous, so the correct answer is the right optic tract.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A person reads a Snellen chart at 6 metres. What happens in the eye when viewing distant objects. [HITEC 26]

options.B: Ciliary muscle relaxes, suspensory ligaments become taut and the lens flattens

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." none of the source options was correct. Distant vision needs relaxation of the ciliary muscle (parasympathetic withdrawal); near vision needs contraction (lens rounds up).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks why transmission is faster from the central retina than from the periphery. What explains this? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Larger nerve fibres in the periphery
options.C: Fewer retinal cells (less convergence) in the central pathway

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fovea." one cone 4 one bipolar 4 one ganglion cell (direct pathway. high acuity); periphery: many rods converge via amacrine cells (slower, more sensitive).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A boy has red-green colour blindness; his maternal grandfather was affected, both parents see normally. What is the inheritance pattern? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The mother is a carrier (from her affected father); each son has a 50A risk. Affected males cannot pass it to sons.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks which retinal neurons f ire action potentials. Which retinal cells transmit signals by action potentials. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Photoreceptors. bipolar and horizontal cells use graded (electrotonic) potentials; ganglion cells (and some amacrine cells) generate action potentials in the optic nerve.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A short-sighted student gets glasses. Which lens corrects myopia. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Myopia ￿ concave (minus); hypermetropia and presbyopia 4 convex (plus); astigmatism 4 cylindrical. Presbyopic myopes may need bifocals/progressive lenses.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old myope cannot read with his distance glasses. Bifocal lenses are commonly used to correct what? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bifocals." upper segment for distance, lower convex segment for near (presbyopic addition).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with long-sightedness strains to read. A convex lens is used to correct which condition? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypermetropia." short eyeball or weak refraction ￿ image behind retina; accommodation compensates in youth (causing eye strain); corrected with convex lenses.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A stroke damages the left optic tract. Which visual field defect results? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left tract carries left temporal + right nasal retinal fibres 4 right visual field of both eyes. Macular sparing suggests an occipital (PCA) lesion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman notices that acidic foods taste sour. What is the mechanism of sour taste transduction. [Prof 24]

options.B: H. ions entering/blocking K. channels, depolarizing the cell

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Salty." Na, via ENaC. Sour." H. via OTOPI channels and block of K. channels. Sweet, bitter, umami: G-protein (gustducin) coupled TIR/T2R receptors PLCF2 4 IP3 4 TRPM5.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a taste disorder is examined. What activates taste buds. [Prof 24. KIMS 26]

options.D: Binding of tastants to receptor cells, causing depolarization (receptor

mcqs.explanation: potential) / Exam Pearl: Taste receptor cells (modified epithelial cells, renewed every~ 10 days) depolarize when tastants dissolved in saliva bind channels/receptors; they synapse with Vll, IX, X fibres ￿ nucleus solitarius ￿ VPM 4 insula.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man enjoys the savoury taste of cheese and broth. Which substance produces the umami taste. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Umami (TIRI + TIR3 receptors) is triggered by L-glutamate (MSG) and enhanced by ribonucleotides (IMP, GMP). Sweet: TIR2+TIR3; bitter." T2R family.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child spits out a bitter medicine. Which substances typically elicit bitter taste. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Sour: H"; salty." Na.; sweet: sugars, glycols, aldehydes, some amino acids,. bitter: alkaloids and long-chain organic substances (protective - many poisons are bitter); umami: glutamate. Bitter has the lowest threshold.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A genetics practical tests students for taste blindness. A person with PTC taste blindness cannot taste which compound? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PTC/PROP tasting depends on TAS2R38 bitter receptor alleles (autosomal dominant tasters)," _30% of people are non-tasters.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student maps taste sensitivity on the tongue. Where is bitter taste detected mainly. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Posterior part of the tongue (circumvallate papillae)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All taste qualities can be detected in all areas, but sensitivity to bitter is greatest at the back (circumvallate, IX) triggering the protective gag/vomiting reflex.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child tastes a tiny amount of a very bitter substance and spits it out immediately. Which property of bitter taste explains this. [HITEC 26]

options.A: It has a very low threshold

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bitter (quinine) has the lowest threshold (~0.000008 M), sour intermediate, salty and sweet (sucrose 0.01 M) the highest - a protective mechanism against toxins.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man loses smell after a viral infection. Where are odorants transduced into electrical signals. [AMC 25]

options.C: Cilia of olfactory receptor neurons (Golf 4 CAMP)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Odorant binds a G-protein (Golf) receptor on cilia 4 adenylyl cyclase 4 CAMP 4 opens cation channels 4 Cl- efflux amplifies depolarization. Receptor neurons are bipolar and regenerate from basal cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist compares sensory pathways. Which sensation reaches the cortex without first relaying in the thalamus. [BWP 26 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Olfactory tract 4 piriform cortex, amygdala, entorhinal cortex directly (a secondary relay via dorsomedial thalamus reaches orbitofrontal cortex). All other senses relay in the thalamus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A histologist examines the olfactory epithelium. What type of cells are olfactory receptor cells. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Olfactory receptor neurons are bipolar. with cilia bearing receptors," their axons form CN I through the cribriform plate. They are replaced every-60 days from basal stem cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man cannot smell after a head injury. What does anosmia mean. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anosmia: absent smell (cribriform plate fracture. viral infection, Kallmann syndrome, Parkinson and Alzheimer disease). Hyposmia = reduced; parosmia = distorted," ageusia = loss of taste.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Olfactory receptor cells are intact but the olfactory glomeruli are damaged. Which function is most likely impaired? [HITEC 26]

options.D: Generation of action potentials in receptor cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each glomerulus receives axons from receptor neurons expressing the same receptor type; the spatial pattern of glomerular activation encodes odour identity (mitral/tufted cells, lateral inhibition by granule cells).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has damage to the olfactory cortex but normal receptors. What is most directly impaired? [BWP 26]

options.D: Conscious perception and identification of smells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary olfactory cortex (piriform, periamygdaloid, entorhinal) and orbitofrontal cortex are needed for conscious discrimination,. receptors and bulb are still functional.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has an olfactory groove meningioma compressing one olfactory tract. Which finding is expected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Foster Kennedy syndrome: ipsilateral anosmia + ipsilateral optic atrophy + contralateral papilloedema (raised ICP) from a frontal/olfactory groove tumour.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with vertigo has damage to the semicircular canals. In the cristae ampullares, the hair cells are embedded in which structure. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cristae (canals) 4 cupula, angular acceleration. Maculae (utricle, saccule) 4 otolithic membrane, linear acceleration/gravity. Organ of Corti tectorial membrane.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a Rinne test, bone conduction is louder than air conduction in a patient's right ear. What does this imply? [Prof 24. BWP 25]

options.A: Sensorineural deafness in the left ear
options.B: Conductive deafness in the right ear
options.D: Sensorineural deafness in the right ear

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rinne negative (BC > AC) = conductive loss in that ear; Weber then lateralizes to the affected ear. In SNHL Rinne stays positive and Weber lateralizes to the better ear.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student learns where lesions cause conductive deafness. Damage up to which point in the auditory pathway causes conductive (not sensorineural) deafness. [HITEC 25]

options.A: External ear, tympanic membrane, ossicles up to the stapes footplate

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reconstructed from handwritten HITEC 25 recall notes. Conductive loss: wax, perforation, otitis media, otosclerosis (stapes fixation). Sensorineural: cochlea (noise, presbycusis, ototoxic drugs), Vlll nerve (acoustic neuroma) and central pathways.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 75-year-old has gradually worsening bilateral hearing loss, especially for high-pitched sounds. What type of hearing loss is presbycusis? [BWP 26 . BWP 25]

options.C: Sensorineural (age-related loss of hair cells at the cochlear base)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Presbycusis: bilateral symmetric high-frequency SNHL starting at the basal turn of the cochlea,. Rinne positive, Weber central.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has dizziness on turning his head; tests suggest a vestibular problem. Which inner ear structure senses angular acceleration. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Three semicircular canals at right angles detect rotation in all planes (cupula deflection); the utricle and saccule sense linear acceleration and head position.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man exposed to loud noise reflexly contracts his middle ear muscles. Which statement describes the attenuation reflex. [QIMS 25]

options.A: It protects against quiet high-frequency sounds
options.B: It increases rigidity of the ossicular system, reducing conduction of low-frequency sound
options.C: It increases low-frequency transmission by 30-40 dB
options.D: It occurs 4-8 seconds after a loud sound

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Stapedius and tensor tympani contract 40-80 ms after loud sound 4 reduce transmission of low frequencies by 30-40 dB; protects the cochlea, masks background noise and reduces hearing of one's own speech.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An audiologist explains place coding of pitch. Which statement about the basilar membrane is correct? [QIMS 25]

options.A: It separates scala media from scala vestibuli
options.B: Its fibres become shorter toward the apex
options.C: It vibrates best at high frequencies near the base and at low
options.D: Its fibre diameter increases toward the apex

mcqs.explanation: frequencies near the apex / Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Basilar fibres are short and stiff at the base (high frequency) and long and flexible at the apex (low frequency). Reissner membrane separates scala vestibuli and media.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a very loud concert, a man has persistent hearing loss and tinnitus. Damage to which structure is responsible. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Noise-induced hearing loss: hair cell damage, typically a notch at 4 kHz on audiometry," sensorineural, irreversible once hair cells die.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student classif ies types of deafness. Sensorineural hearing loss is due to damage to which structure. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SNHL: inner ear (hair cells) or Vlll nerve/central pathway; Rinne positive (AC > BC), Weber to the better ear. Conductive: outer/middle ear.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies pitch discrimination. Low-frequency sounds maximally vibrate the basilar membrane at which site. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Place principle: high frequencies near the base (stiff, narrow fibres), low frequencies near the apex (wide, flexible fibres); the travelling wave peaks at the characteristic place.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks where mechanical sound energy becomes nerve signals. Where does sound transduction occur in the cochlea. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Basilar membrane movement bends stereocilia against the tectorial membrane ￿ tip-link opening ￿ K. influx from endolymph 4 depolarization glutamate release onto spiral ganglion neurons.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has damage to the basilar membrane of the cochlea. Which function is most directly impaired? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Place theory: the basilar membrane acts as a frequency analyser; tuned outer hair cells (prestin) amplify and sharpen the response.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks why hair cells depolarize when stereocilia bend toward the kinocilium. Which ion moves from endolymph into stereocilia to depolarize the hair cell? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endolymph has high K, (~ 150 mm) and +80 mv endocochlear potential (stria vascularis); K, enters through mechanotransduction channels and depolarizes the cell (unusual - K. influx).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks which receptor detects forward acceleration in a car. Linear acceleration is detected by which structure. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: vertical acceleration. Cristae Exam Pearl: Utricle macula (horizontal) horizontal linear acceleration and head tilt," saccule macula (vertical) angular.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The ossicles vibrate normally but energy is poorly transmitted into the cochlear fluid. Stiffness at which structure could cause this. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Impedance matching: the TM:oval window area ratio (-17: 1) and ossicular lever (- 1.3) raise pressure~22x to move cochlear fluid. Otosclerosis fixes the stapes footplate in the oval window.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has unilateral sensorineural hearing loss. To which side does the Weber test lateralize. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Weber." SNHL 4 better ear." conductive loss ￿ affected ear (masking of ambient noise). Combine with Rinne (BC > AC = conductive).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A young woman has progressive hearing loss worsening in pregnancy; Rinne is negative. Which is a classic cause of conductive (not sensorineural) hearing loss? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Otosclerosis." autosomal dominant, new spongy bone fixes the stapes footplate; Carhart notch at 2 kHz; treated by stapedectomy or hearing aids.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student lists receptors for each sensation. Which sensation has free nerve endings as its receptors. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Nociceptors are free nerve endings (AS and C fibres) that adapt very little. Taste and smell use chemoreceptor cells; vision uses rods and cones. ENDOCRINOLOGY

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has palpitations, weight loss and heat intolerance. Which thyroid hormone is the most active form at the tissues. [Prof 24. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid secretes mostly T4 (~ 93%), but T3 is 3-4x more potent and binds nuclear receptors with higher affinity; peripheral 5-deiodinase converts T44T3.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A tumour compresses the pituitary stalk and median eminence. Which anterior pituitary hormone does NOT fall and may rise. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prolactin is under tonic inhibition by hypothalamic dopamine," stalk section removes it ("stalk effect") 4 hyperprolactinaemia while other anterior pituitary hormones fall.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman has exophthalmos, tremor and a diffuse goitre. What are the TSH and T3n4 levels in Graves disease? [Prof 24. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Graves: TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies (TSI) drive the gland 4 high T3tr4 that suppress pituitary TSH. Exophthalmos and pretibial myxoedema are specific to Graves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has weight gain, lethargy, cold intolerance, constipation and loss of interest in her surroundings. What is the diagnosis. [Prof 24. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypothyroidism: l BMR 4 weight gain. cold intolerance, bradycardia. dry skin, menorrhagia, slow-relaxing reflexes, myxoedema: commonest cause Hashimoto thyroiditis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy has excessive thirst and passes large volumes of urine. Polyuria and polydipsia are cardinal features of which conditions. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DM." osmotic diuresis (glucose) 4 hyperosmolar urine with glucose. DI: ADH deficiency/resistance 4 large volumes of dilute urine. Water deprivation and desmopressin tests distinguish central from nephrogenic DI.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After thyroidectomy, a patient has perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm. Which condition explains the low serum calcium. [Prof 24. HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Accidental removal/devascularization of parathyroids ￿ I PTH 4 hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia 4 tetany (Chvostek, Trousseau signs)," treat with IV calcium gluconate, then calcium + calcitriol.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has hypertension, hypokalaemia and low plasma renin; CT shows an adrenal adenoma of the zona glomerulosa. What is the diagnosis? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary aldosteronism: high aldosterone, low renin (raised ARR), hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis, little oedema (aldosterone escape). Secondary aldosteronism has high renin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has a functioning thyroid tumour secreting excess hormone. What is the usual pattern of T3 and T4 levels. [Prof 24]

options.B: Both raised, with a raised T3:T4 ratio

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In hyperthyroidism T3 rises proportionally more than T4 (increased deiodination and preferential T3 secretion); "T3 toxicosis" may occur with normal T4.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student's blood is sampled after vigorous exercise. Which hormone rises markedly after exercise. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GH secretion t . deep sleep (stage 3), exercise, stress, hypoglycaemia, fasting, amino acids (arginine), ghrelin. I . hyperglycaemia, somatostatin, IGF-I, obesity, glucocorticoids.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with fatigue and weight gain also has heavy menstrual bleeding. Which endocrine disorder classically causes menorrhagia. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypothyroidism: menorrhagia (anovulation, t prolactin). constipation, cold intolerance, weight gain. Hyperthyroidism." oligomenorrhoea, hyperdefecation, weight loss.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with polyuria has a water deprivation test: urine osmolality stays low, but rises markedly after desmopressin. Where is the defect? [KIMS 26 . WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Central DI: lack of ADH, responds to desmopressin. Nephrogenic DI (lithium, hypercalcaemia, V2/AQP2 mutations): no response. Primary polydipsia." concentrates urine on water deprivation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A young woman has tachycardia, fine tremor of the hands, sweating and weight loss. What is the most likely cause. [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid hormone t BMR, sensitizes tissues to catecholamines ( t F-receptors) 4 tachycardia, tremor, heat intolerance, weight loss with increased appetite.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks what ADH does in the kidney. What is the main action of ADH? [BWP 25]

options.B: Water reabsorption in the collecting ducts (fluid/osmolality balance)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADH 4 V2 receptors (Gs, CAMP) 4 insertion of aquaporin-2 4 concentrated urine; at high levels Vl receptors cause vasoconstriction (vasopressin).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has tremor, insomnia and restlessness. Which is the best first screening test for thyroid dysfunction. [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TSH is the most sensitive single test (log-linear relation with free T4). Low TSH 4 measure free T4tr3; TSI confirms Graves; scan distinguishes causes.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with hypothyroidism is examined. Which reflex finding is typical? [BWP 26. BWP 25]

options.A: Slow relaxation phase of the ankle jerk

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Delayed relaxation ("hung-up") reflexes are characteristic of hypothyroidism; pendular knee jerk = cerebellar disease; clonus = UMN lesion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies how GH stimulates growth. The actions of GH are mediated in part by which substances. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied.. the source gave no answer key. GH 4 liver IGF-I (somatomedin C) ￿ growth of cartilage, bone, muscle. GH directly causes lipolysis and anti-insulin effects. Laron dwarfism: GH receptor defect (high GH, low IGF-I).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has a stroke causing necrosis of the posterior pituitary. Which effect is most likely. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Loss of ADH 4 large volumes of dilute urine ￿ hypernatraemia if water intake is inadequate. Lactation needs prolactin (anterior) only milk ejection (oxytocin) would be impaired.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies how GH increases long-bone length. On which cells does GH (via IGF-I) act to cause long-bone growth? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. GH/IGF-I stimulate proliferation of epiphyseal chondrocytes," once the plates fuse (estrogen-dependent). excess GH causes acromegaly rather than gigantism.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student tests GH secretion under different conditions. Which condition suppresses GH secretion. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Hyperglycaemia suppresses GH (basis of the OGTh suppression test for acromegaly),. deep sleep, exercise. fasting, hypoglycaemia and arginine stimulate it. (Somatostatin is a hormone that also inhibits GH.)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student compares pituitary dwarfism with cretinism. Which feature is seen in pituitary dwarfism but not typically in cretinism? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Pituitary dwarf: proportionate, normal intelligence, may have hypoglycaemia (no GH counter-regulation). Cretin." mental retardation, coarse features, macroglossia, delayed bone age, umbilical hernia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with Graves disease has blood tests. Which level is decreased in Graves disease. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. TSI drives excess T3tt4, which suppress TSH from the pituitary and TRH from the hypothalamus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies hypothalamic control of GH. Which factor inhibits GH secretion by the anterior pituitary. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Somatostatin (GHIH) from the periventricular nucleus inhibits GH and TSH release; octreotide is used to treat acromegaly.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has puffy skin and lethargy. His plasma TSH is low but rises markedly after TRH injection. What is the diagnosis. [HITEC 26. QIMS 25]

options.A: Hypothyroidism due to a hypothalamic abnormality
options.B: Hypothyroidism due to a thyroid abnormality
options.C: Hypothyroidism due to a pituitary abnormality
options.D: Hyperthyroidism due to a thyroid tumour

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. TRH test: pituitary failure ￿ no TSH rise; hypothalamic failure ￿ TSH rises (pituitary intact)," primary thyroid failure 4 high basal TSH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student asks which hormone is both synthesized and stored in the pituitary. Which is it? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Anterior pituitary hormones (GH, PRL, ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH) are synthesized and stored there. Vasopressin and oxytocin are synthesized in the hypothalamus and only stored in the posterior pituitary.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has weight loss with increased appetite, palpitations, heat intolerance, diffuse goitre and exophthalmos. What is the diagnosis? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Graves." autoimmune (TSI), diffuse goitre with bruit, ophthalmopathy (retro-orbital fibroblast activation). pretibial myxoedema," commonest cause of hyperthyroidism in young women.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child has proportionate short stature, low IGF-I and a poor GH response to stimulation tests. What is the most likely diagnosis. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GH deficiency: proportionate short stature, delayed bone age, normal intelligence, chubby appearance, hypoglycaemia in infancy," failure of GH rise after insulin/arginine/glucagon stimulation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has decreased BMR, weight gain and sluggishness. Which condition is suggested? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid hormone sets BMR by increasing Na'/K'_ATPase activity, mitochondrial number and oxygen consumption; hypothyroid BMR may fall to 40-50A of normal.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has resistant hypertension, muscle weakness and low potassium. What does Conn syndrome typically cause. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Excess aldosterone 4 Na, retention (hypertension), K, and H, loss (hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis), suppressed renin. Hyperpigmentation and hyperkalaemia are features of Addison disease.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man drinks large amounts of water and passes large volumes of dilute urine. Which condition does this suggest? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DI: urine osmolality <300 mOsm/kg, high serum osmolality; DM causes polyuria with glycosuria (osmotic, not dilute)," SIADH causes concentrated urine with hyponatraemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with acromegaly has markedly raised GH. Which metabolic change is most likely. [MUL 26]

options.A: Increased glucose use by adipose tissue
options.D: Increased glucose uptake by skeletal muscle

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GH is anabolic for protein but diabetogenic: t lipolysis and fatty acid use, I peripheral glucose uptake (insulin resistance), t hepatic glucose output hyperglycaemia in ~30% of acromegalics.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman fails to lactate and has amenorrhoea after severe postpartum haemorrhage; months later she has fatigue, low cortisol, low free T4 and low estradiol. Which hormonal finding fits her condition. [MUL 26. BWP 26]

options.A: Low ACTH with increased CRH (loss of feedback)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sheehan syndrome: ischaemic necrosis of the enlarged pregnant pituitary 4 panhypopituitarism (failure of lactation first). Low ACTH 4 low cortisol; hypothalamic CRH rises because negative feedback is lost," no hyperpigmentation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old has rapid growth, enlarged hands and feet and high IGF-I, with open epiphyses. Which mechanism most directly causes the linear growth? [HITEC 26]

options.C: IGF-l-mediated chondrocyte proliferation at epiphyseal plates

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Before epiphyseal closure, GH excess ￿ gigantism (linear growth); after closure 4 acromegaly (bone thickening, soft tissue growth).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old has an enlarged jaw, spaced teeth and enlarged hands after epiphyseal closure. What is the diagnosis. [HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Acromegaly: prognathism. frontal bossing, macroglossia. spade hands, sweating, carpal tunnel, diabetes, hypertension, cardiomyopathy; confirm with IGF-I and failure of GH suppression on OGTT.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with Graves disease has tachycardia, tremor and palpitations. Which mechanism contributes most? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid hormone upregulates Fl receptors and Na'/K'_ATPase; propranolol relieves symptoms and reduces T4 4 T3 conversion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with panhypopituitarism has severe GH, TSH and ACTH deficiency. Which combination is expected? [HITEC 26]

options.A: Decreased growth, reduced BMR, impaired fasting glucose
options.B: Increased growth, BMR and hypertension maintenance and fatigue

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Order of loss in compressive pituitary lesions: GH 4 FSH/LH 4 TSH 4 ACTH ( Go Look For The Adenoma") 4 prolactin may rise (stalk effect).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman has renal colic, recurrent UTIS, weakness and bone pain; calcium is high and phosphate low. Which disorder is most likely. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "Stones, bones, abdominal groans and psychic moans": parathyroid adenoma (85%) 4 hypercalcaemia, hypophosphataemia. T PTH, t urinary calcium, osteitis fibrosa cystica.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An 8-year-old is the shortest in his class; body proportions are normal and examination is otherwise unremarkable. Which condition is most likely [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proportionate short stature with normal health suggests GH deficiency (or constitutional/familial short stature),. hypothyroidism gives infantile proportions (high upper:lower ratio) and mental slowing.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child is severely dehydrated from vomiting and diarrhoea. Which immediate hormonal response best combats this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypovolaemia and hyperosmolality 4 ADH t (water retention), renin-angiotensin-aldosterone t (Na" retention). thirst t . ANP falls.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has increased BMR, heat intolerance and weight loss despite increased appetite. Which action explains the increased BMR? [KIMS 26]

options.D: Increased cellular oxidative metabolism by T3/T4 ( t Na'/K'_ATPase,

mcqs.explanation: mitochondria) / Exam Pearl: T3 increases the number and activity of mitochondria and Na'/K'_ATPase pumps 4 t 02 consumption and heat production in most tissues (not brain, spleen, gonads).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman is evaluated for infertility by hysterosalpingography. Where does fertilization normally take place? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fertilization occurs in the ampulla within -24 h of ovulation." the zygote reaches the uterus at the morula stage (day 4) and implants-day 6-7. Ampulla is also the commonest site of ectopic pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After conception, the corpus luteum must survive beyond 14 days. Which hormone rescues the corpus luteum and maintains early pregnancy. [Prof 24. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: hCG (LH-like a/F glycoprotein) appears ~day 8-9, peaks at 10- 12 weeks; keeps the corpus luteum secreting progesterone until the placenta takes over (luteo-placental shift-8-10 weeks).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman in the second trimester notices breast enlargement. Which hormone mainly causes growth of the lobules and alveoli of the breast? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Estrogen 4 ductal growth and fat deposition; progesterone 4 lobule-alveolar development and secretory capacity; prolactin 4 milk synthesis (blocked by high estrogen/progesterone until delivery)." oxytocin 4 ejection.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man has low testosterone and infertility. Which testicular cells secrete testosterone. [Prof 24. CKMC 26. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LH 4 Leydig cells 4 testosterone. FSH 4 Sertoli cells 4 ABP, inhibin. AMH, support spermatogenesis." Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
