mcqs.question: During fertilization, the sperm must pass through the cell layer around the oocyte. What is the function of sperm hyaluronidase. [Prof 24]

options.C: Digests hyaluronic acid between corona radiata cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corona radiata: hyaluronidase. Zona pellucida: acrosin and proteolytic enzymes after the acrosome reaction (triggered by ZP3). Cortical reaction and zona reaction prevent polyspermy.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A tall young man has gynaecomastia, small firm testes and azoospermia. What is the most likely cause. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Klinefelter: seminiferous tubule dysgenesis ￿ 1 inhibin ( t FSH), Leydig dysfunction (I testosterone, t LH, t estradiol) ￿ gynaecomastia, eunuchoid habitus, infertility.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old boy enters puberty. What is a primary function of testosterone. [AMC 25]

options.C: Development of male secondary sexual characteristics and

mcqs.explanation: spermatogenesis / Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Testosterone." Wolffian duct development, spermatogenesis (with FSH), libido, muscle mass, voice deepening, epiphyseal closure (via estradiol). DHT: external genitalia, prostate, hair, acne.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A mother starts producing copious milk on the third day after delivery. What allows lactation to begin only after delivery. [AMC 25 . QIMS 25]

options.B: Fall in estrogen and progesterone allowing prolactin to act

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prolactin rises throughout pregnancy, but high placental estrogen and progesterone block its lactogenic action," after delivery of the placenta they fall and milk secretion begins (lactogenesis11).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman in labour has increasingly strong contractions as the head stretches the cervix. Which hormone mainly increases uterine contractility during labour. [CKMC 26. AMC 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cervical stretch 4 neural signals to hypothalamus ￿ oxytocin t 4 stronger contractions 4 more stretch (positive feedback). Oxytocin receptors in the myometrium increase near term; prostaglandins also stimulate contraction.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man receiving testicular irradiation becomes infertile but keeps normal testosterone levels. Which testicular cells are relatively resistant to radiation? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dividing germ cells (spermatogonia) are highly radiosensitive," Leydig and Sertoli cells are resistant, so androgen production persists after doses that cause azoospermia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A mother asks which hormone makes her breasts produce milk. Which hormone stimulates milk production (synthesis)? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Prolactin (lactotrophs, acidophils) stimulates milk protein, lactose and fat synthesis," suckling maintains it by inhibiting dopamine release. Oxytocin causes milk ejection.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A breastfeeding mother notices milk spurting from the other breast when the baby suckles. Which hormone causes milk ejection (let-down)? [AMC 26. CKMC 26. HITEC 26. KIMS 26. WMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Suckling ￿ afferents 4 paraventricular/supraoptic nuclei ￿ oxytocin ￿ contraction of myoepithelial cells around alveoli. Let-down can be triggered by the baby's cry and inhibited by stress.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student plots testosterone levels across a man's lifespan. During which period is testosterone secretion negligible. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Testosterone is high in fetal life (placental hCG), briefly after birth ("mini-puberty"), negligible through childhood, rises at puberty and falls slowly after 50. Key note: source options lacked "childhood"

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A breastfeeding mother has no periods for several months. What is the cause of lactational amenorrhoea. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Suckling-induced prolactin suppresses GnRH pulsatility 4 low FSH/LH 4 no ovulation; contraceptive effect is unreliable once feeds become infrequent.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman develops gestational diabetes in the third trimester. Which hormone mainly causes insulin resistance in pregnancy? [KIMS 26. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: hPL (somatomammotropin) GH-like and prolactin-like: maternal insulin resistance, lipolysis, glucose sparing for the fetus. Progesterone, cortisol and placental GH also contribute.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies testicular endocrine control. On which cells do FSH and LH act in the male. [BWP 26. BWP 25]

options.A: FSH on Sertoli cells; LH on Leydig cells
options.C: FSH on Leydig; LH on Sertoli

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LH 4 Leydig ￿ testosterone (negative feedback on LH). FSH + high intratesticular testosterone 4 Sertoli ￿ spermatogenesis, ABP, inhibin (negative feedback on FSH).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with oligomenorrhoea and multiple small ovarian follicles has excessive follicular atresia. Which hormonal pattern causes this. [BWP 25]

options.C: High LH with low/normal FSH (raised LH:FSH ratio)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCOS: t LH 4 theca androgen excess," relatively low FSH 4 poor aromatization in granulosa cells 4 follicular arrest/atresia, anovulation, hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a non-fertile cycle, the corpus luteum degenerates about 12 days after ovulation. What causes its involution. [QIMS 25]

options.B: High estrogen (and progesterone) suppressing LH secretion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Guyton: estrogen and progesterone (with inhibin) from the corpus luteum inhibit FSH/LH," without LH support it involutes ￿ falling steroids 4 menstruation. hCG rescues it in pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student plots hormone levels in the menstrual cycle. When does progesterone reach its highest level? [QIMS 25]

options.B: Between ovulation and the start of menstruation (mid-luteal phase)
options.D: When LH is at its peak

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Progesterone peaks -day 21 (7 days after ovulation) - measured to confirm ovulation; it raises basal body temperature-0.5 °C and makes the endometrium secretory.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Seven days after ovulation, pituitary LH secretion falls. What causes this decrease. [QIMS 25]

options.A: The pituitary becomes unresponsive to GnRH
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone from the corpus luteum suppress GnRH andLH

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Combined negative feedback by luteal estrogen + progesterone (and inhibin A) keeps FSH and LH low during the luteal phase.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After birth, pulmonary artery pressure falls sharply. Why. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Pulmonary vascular resistance decreases as the lungs expand and

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Lung expansion and t alveolar O, dilate pulmonary vessels 4 PVR falls~5-fold," systemic resistance rises (placenta removed): foramen ovale closes functionally, ductus closes within days.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman in preterm labour is studied. Which agent could inhibit the initiation of labour? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Progesterone inhibits uterine contractility ( I gap junctions, l oxytocin receptors); the estrogen:progesterone ratio rises near term. Cervical stretch and oxytocin promote labour.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman receives daily injections from day 16 of her cycle and does not menstruate while the injections continue. What is the injected substance. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. hCG mimics LH, maintaining the corpus luteum and its progesterone/estrogen output 4 no endometrial shedding (as in early pregnancy).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A professional female athlete has had no periods for 5 years but her bone density is normal. Which fact may explain these observations. [QIMS 25]

options.A: She has been taking anabolic (androgenic) steroids
options.D: Her estrogen is very low (would cause osteoporosis)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Androgens suppress GnRH/LH/FSH (amenorrhoea) yet preserve bone (directly and via aromatization). Hypothalamic (athletic) amenorrhoea with low estrogen would reduce bone density.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has raised FSH but normal LH and testosterone after chemotherapy damaged his Sertoli cells. Which hormone normally selectively suppresses FSH? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inhibin B (Sertoli cells, granulosa cells) selectively inhibits FSH; testosterone/estradiol inhibit LH (and GnRH). Isolated t FSH = marker of impaired spermatogenesis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: At the end of a non~fertile cycle, menstruation begins. Which hormonal change triggers menstruation. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Fall in progesterone (and estrogen) as the corpus luteum regresses

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Steroid withdrawal 4 spiral artery vasospasm (prostaglandins) 4 ischaemic necrosis of the functional layer 4 shedding,. the basal layer regenerates the endometrium.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A biopsy taken on day 22 of the cycle is examined. What is the endometrium like in the luteal phase. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]

options.D: Thickened and secretory (tortuous glands with glycogen)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Follicular (estrogen)." proliferative phase with straight glands and mitoses. Luteal (progesterone): secretory phase - coiled glands, subnuclear then luminal glycogen vacuoles, stromal oedema, spiral arteries.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A girl starts puberty with breast development. What is estrogen responsible for? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Estrogen." breast ducts, female fat distribution, uterine and vaginal growth, proliferative endometrium. LH surge (positive feedback), epiphyseal closure, t HDL, bone protection.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student compares hormone levels in a breastfeeding mother with those in late pregnancy. Which hormonal pattern is typical in a lactating woman. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: After delivery progesterone and estrogen fall abruptly," suckling keeps prolactin high (bursts with each feed) and suppresses GnRH ￿ lactational amenorrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes steroid hormones. Which hormone primarily supports corpus luteum function in the luteal phase. [MUL 26]

options.A: LH, stimulating progesterone and estradiol secretion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Basal LH maintains the corpus luteum for- 14 days,. luteinized granulosa and theca cells produce progesterone, estradiol and inhibin A. In pregnancy hCG replaces LH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman is threatened with miscarriage in early pregnancy. Which hormone maintains the endometrium (decidua) during pregnancy. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Progesterone ("pro~gestation") maintains the decidua, keeps the myometrium quiet and cervix closed; from corpus luteum until -8- 10 weeks, then from the placenta.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with impaired Sertoli cell function has reduced sperm production. Deficiency of which hormone could cause this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: FSH acts on Sertoli cells 4 androgen-binding protein (keeps testosterone high in tubules), inhibin, nutrients for spermatogenesis. LH acts on Leydig cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Sperm in the female tract cannot fertilize the ovum until they undergo functional changes. Which process prepares sperm for fertilization. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Capacitation (5-6 h in the female tract): removal of cholesterol and glycoproteins from the sperm head membrane, hyperactivated motility, enabling the acrosome reaction at the zona pellucida.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old woman with regular cycles presents with two years of subfertility. Which investigation should be ordered first? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Male factor contributes to ~40A of infertility and semen analysis is simple and non-invasive; with regular cycles ovulation is likely (confirm with day-21 progesterone).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman one month postpartum, breastfeeding, wants short-term contraception. Which option is most appropriate? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Estrogen reduces milk supply and raises thrombosis risk postpartum, so combined pills are avoided while breastfeeding (<6 months). Progestogen-only methods or barrier methods are suitable; source wanted a short-term method.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has low serum progesterone on day 21 of a regular cycle. Dysfunction of which structure is most likely. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mid~luteal progesterone >30 nmol/L confirms ovulation; low levels indicate anovulation or inadequate corpus luteum (luteal phase defect).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has amenorrhoea, hot flushes and vaginal dryness, with low estrogen and high FSH and LH. What is the diagnosis. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Depletion of follicles 4 l estrogen and inhibin 4 loss of negative feedback ￿ t FSH (earliest and most marked) and LH. Hypothalamic amenorrhoea has low FSH/LH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has a thin, atrophic endometrium with scanty irregular bleeding. Deficiency of which hormone most directly explains this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Estrogen drives endometrial proliferation (follicular phase); progesterone acts on an estrogen-primed endometrium. Unopposed estrogen causes hyperplasia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A mother who recently delivered produces milk but has poor let-down. Deficiency of which hormone explains this? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Milk production (prolactin) and ejection (oxytocin) are separate; pain, anxiety and alcohol inhibit oxytocin release and let-down.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 23-year-old man has infertility, low testosterone, delayed puberty and low LH and FSH. What is the most likely diagnosis. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low gonadotropins + low testosterone = hypothalamic/pituitary cause (Kallmann, tumour, hyperprolactinaemia); high gonadotropins + low testosterone = primary testicular failure (Klinefelter).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies Sertoli cell function. Which hormone stimulates Sertoli cells to synthesize androgen-binding protein. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ABP concentrates testosterone in seminiferous tubules and epididymis - essential for spermatogenesis. FSH also stimulates inhibin B and aromatase in Sertoli cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman uses the combined oral contraceptive pill. How do estrogen and progesterone prevent pregnancy. [BWP 26]

options.A: They suppress gonadotropin secretion and inhibit ovulation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Negative feedback on GnRH/FSH/LH prevents follicle development and the mid-cycle LH surge,. progestogen also thickens cervical mucus and makes the endometrium unreceptive.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman has maternal serum screening. Which hormone is commonly used as a marker in maternal serum screening of fetal well-being. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Triple/quadruple test: AFP, hCG, unconjugated estriol (+ inhibin A). Down syndrome: t hCG, t inhibin, l AFP, l estriol. Source prompt was broad.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with abdominal pain has a raised hCG and a mass in the fallopian tube. What is the most likely diagnosis? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ectopic pregnancy (ampulla commonest)." amenorrhoea, pain, vaginal bleeding; hCG rises slower than normal and no intrauterine sac is seen when hCG >1500-2000 IU/L. Risk: PID, previous ectopic, tubal surgery.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies fetal circulation. Which fetal vessel carries the most oxygenated blood? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Umbilical vein (PO, -30 mmHg, ~80% saturation) 4 ductus venosus ￿ IVC 4 foramen ovale ￿ left heart ￿ brain. Fetal Hb (higher O, affinity) aids uptake.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman is on hormonal contraception; ultrasound shows no ovulation. Which hormonal change most directly inhibits ovulation. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ovulation follows the LH surge by-36 h (peak 10-12 h before)," preventing the surge (COC, high progesterone, hyperprolactinaemia) blocks ovulation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old infertile man has high LH and FSH and markedly low testosterone. Where is the lesion. [KIMS 26]

options.D: Testis (Leydig and germ cells) - primary hypogonadism

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary (hypergonadotropic) hypogonadism: testicular failure with loss of negative feedback (Klinefelter, orchitis, chemotherapy). Low testosterone with low LH/FSH = secondary (hypogonadotropic).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studies the trigger for ovulation. What directly triggers the LH surge in a normal cycle. [KIMS 26]

options.A: Sustained high estrogen from the dominant follicle (positive feedback)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl. Estradiol >200 pg/mL for-36-48 h switches feedback from negative to positive at the hypothalamus/pituitary 4 LH surge (with a smaller FSH surge) ovulation 36 h later.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student lists cardiovascular changes in normal pregnancy. Which parameter is classically decreased? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Progesterone, NO and the low-resistance placenta reduce SVR 4 BP falls in the second trimester; blood volume (+40-50%). cardiac output (+30-50%), HR and stroke volume increase.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student explains the hormonal basis of the onset of labour. Which statement is correct? [KIMS 26]

options.B: Estrogen dominates over progesterone at term
options.C: Progesterone peaks at term and triggers labour
options.D: Fetal pituitary secretes large amounts of oxytocin

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Near term the estrogen:progesterone ratio rises (functional progesterone withdrawal), increasing oxytocin receptors, gap junctions and prostaglandins: fetal cortisol (and placental CRH) promote this.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Within minutes of birth, flow through the foramen ovale stops. What is the primary cause. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lung expansion 4 I PVR ￿ t pulmonary venous return ￿ t LA pressure," placental removal 4 I IVC return ￿ l RA pressure ￿ the flap valve (septum primum) closes,. anatomical fusion over months.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tumour shows overexpression of a growth-promoting gene that is also present in normal cells. In which cells are proto-oncogenes found? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proto-oncogenes are normal genes for growth factors, receptors, signal transducers (RAS), transcription factors (MYC) and cell-cycle regulators; gain-of-function mutation/amplification/translocation converts them to oncogenes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man has altered bowel habits and iron-deficiency anaemia; colonoscopy shows a mass. Which tumour marker is used to monitor colorectal cancer. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CEA: colorectal (also pancreas, stomach, lung, breast) - mainly for follow-up and recurrence, not screening. CA-125." ovary; AFP: hepatocellular carcinoma, yolk sac tumours; PSA: prostate; CA 19-9: pancreas," hCG: choriocarcinoma.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tumour larger than 2 mm continues to grow by forming new blood vessels. What is the role of increased VEGF? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hallmarks of cancer include sustained angiogenesis (VEGF, FGF; HIF-la under hypoxia). Bevacizumab is an anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Tumour cells take up large amounts of glucose and produce lactate even in the presence of oxygen. Which hallmark of cancer does this Warburg effect represent? [MUL 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aerobic glycolysis supplies intermediates for biosynthesis (nucleotides, lipids, amino acids) and is the basis of FDG-PET imaging. Driven by MYC, HIF-la, P13K/Akt, loss of p53.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A family has sarcomas, breast cancer and leukaemia at young ages; a germline TP53 mutation is found. How does loss of p53 promote cancer. [LHR 25. QIMS 25]

options.A: Loss of cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis after DNA damage

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: p53 ("guardian of the genome") induces p21 (Gl arrest), DNA repair or apoptosis (BAX. PUMA). Li-Fraumeni syndrome: germline TP53 mutation. MDM2 degrades p53; HPV E6 inactivates it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old woman has abdominal distension, ascites and an adnexal mass. Which tumour marker is raised in ovarian epithelial cancer. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CA-125." serous ovarian carcinoma (also raised in endometriosis. PID, pregnancy). Used for monitoring and, with ultrasound, in the RMI score.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A carcinoma invades through the basement membrane into surrounding stroma. Which enzymes do cancer cells use to degrade the extracellular matrix. [HITEC 26. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Invasion: loss of E-cadherin 4 detachment: MMPS (collagenase IV) degrade basement membrane: integrins attach to new matrix; then intravasation and metastasis. Caspases execute apoptosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman's breast cancer shows HER2/neu gene amplification and is treated with trastuzumab. What is the effect of HER2 amplification. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increased growth factor receptor signalling (tyrosine kinase)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. HER2 (ERBB2) is a growth-factor receptor tyrosine kinase oncogene amplified in -20A of breast cancers 4 aggressive tumours." trastuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man with weight loss, jaundice and hepatomegaly is evaluated. Which tumour marker is most useful? [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. AFP.. hepatocellular carcinoma, yolk sac tumour, (also raised in pregnancy with neural tube defects). Raised in cirrhosis/hepatitis B background of HCC.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A carcinoma begins to metastasize. Which adhesion molecules are reduced, allowing tumour cells to detach? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of E-cadherin (epithelial-mesenchymal transition) allows detachment,. integrins and laminin receptors mediate attachment to the matrix." selectins aid haematogenous spread.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A Burkitt lymphoma has a t(8;14) translocation activating MYC. How does MYC promote cancer. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. MYC is a nuclear transcription factor that activates cyclins, ribosome biogenesis and aerobic glycolysis (Warburg).. N-MYC is amplified in neuroblastoma.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A PET scan shows tumour cells avidly taking up glucose despite adequate oxygen. Why do cancer cells rely heavily on glycolysis. [AMC 26]

options.A: To produce more ATP per glucose
options.D: To provide intermediates for biosynthesis of new cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aerobic glycolysis (Warburg) yields less ATP per glucose but supplies carbon for nucleotides (via HMP shunt), amino acids and lipids, and NADPH," driven by oncogenes and hypoxia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cancer cell produces a microRNA that reduces the MRNA of a tumour-suppressor gene. Which mechanism does this describe. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oncogenic miRNAs ("oncomiRs") silence tumour suppressors without changing DNA sequence," epigenetic changes also include promoter hypermethylation (e.g. MLH I) and histone modification.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with leukaemia receives methotrexate. Synthesis of which molecules does methotrexate impair. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase 4 l THF ￿ I purine and dTMP synthesis 4 arrests rapidly dividing (S-phase) cells," leucovorin rescue.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A pathologist discusses the most commonly mutated gene in human cancers. Which gene is called the "guardian of the genome" [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TP53 (chromosome 17p) is mutated in >50% of cancers. RB (13q) is the "governor" of the GI/S checkpoint.. RAS and MYC are oncogenes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman treated for ovarian carcinoma has serial tumour-marker measurements to assess response and recurrence. Which glycoprotein is used? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CA-125 (MUC16) is raised in -80% of epithelial ovarian cancers - most useful for monitoring," less specific for screening (raised in endometriosis, PID, pregnancy, menstruation).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tumour has persistent activation of a small GTPase and a defect preventing a stress-responsive protein from inducing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. Which combination fits. [MUL 26]

options.A: Loss of RAS and activation of TP53
options.B: Activation of RB and loss of RAS
options.C: Loss of RB and activation of RAS only
options.D: Activation of RAS and loss of TP53

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RAS (GTPase) mutations lock it in the GTP-bound active state (impaired GTPase), e.g. KRAS in pancreatic/colon cancer; TP53 loss removes the DNA-damage checkpoint - a classic multistep carcinogenesis pair.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tumour-suppressor gene is silenced in a cancer cell although its DNA sequence is intact. Which epigenetic mechanism is most directly responsible. [MUL 26 . HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNMTS methylate cytosines in promoter CpG islands 4 MeCP proteins recruit histone deacetylases 4 silent chromatin (e.g. MLHI in sporadic MSI colon cancer, BRCAI, p16). Global hypomethylation causes genomic instability.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A carcinoma develops distant metastases. Which change most directly facilitates invasion of the surrounding extracellular matrix. [MUL 26]

options.A: Increased MMP~2 and MMP-9 (type IV collagenase) activity

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MMP-2 and MMP-9 degrade type IV collagen of the basement membrane," tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPS) oppose them. EMT and loss of E-cadherin enable detachment first.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A young man has a testicular mass and raised serum AFP. Which tumour marker is typically elevated in hepatocellular carcinoma and germ-cell (yolk sac) tumours? [HITEC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AFP: HCC, yolk sac tumour (pure seminoma never raises AFP). hCG: choriocarcinoma, some seminomas. LDH: tumour bulk.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student classifies cancer genes. Which type of gene, when mutated, leads to uncontrolled growth by failing to inhibit proliferation. [HITEC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tumour suppressors (TP53, RB, APC, BRCA1/2, NFI, WTI) are recessive at the cellular level - both alleles must be lost (Knudson two-hit). Oncogenes are dominant (one allele activated).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has hepatomegaly and markedly raised AFP from hepatocellular carcinoma. Which biochemical finding reflects the metabolic behaviour of the tumour. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tumour cells (Warburg effect) convert much glucose to lactate even with oxygen," raised LDH and lactate are common in advanced malignancy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A pancreatic cancer has a KRAS mutation. Why does RAS activation lead to cancer. [BWP 26]

options.C: It promotes persistent growth-factor signalling (GTP~bound RAS)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mutant RAS loses GTPase activity (or GAP sensitivity) 4 stays GTP-bound ￿ RAF-MEK-ERK and P13K-Akt signalling 4 proliferation. Commonest oncogene mutation in human cancer.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has a rapidly growing jaw tumour with starry-sky histology and t(8;14). With which virus is Burkitt lymphoma associated? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oncogenic viruses: EBV (Burkitt, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Hodgkin), HPV 16/18 (cervix - E6 inactivates p53, E7 inactivates RB), HB V/HCV (HCC), HTLV-I (adult T-cell leukaemia), HHV-8 (Kaposi).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A recalled question linked microsatellite DNA with MYC protein. When MYC binds its target DNA (E~box) sequences, which effect results. [BWP 26]

options.D: Altered transcriptional regulation and gene expression

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MYC-MAX heterodimers bind E-boxes (CACGTG) and activate genes for growth, ribosome biogenesis and glycolysis. Source stem was unclear; reconstructed around MYC transcriptional action.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks why the lungs are a common site of blood-borne metastases. Which characteristic of the lungs explains this. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Extensive capillary network receiving all venous return

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lungs (all systemic venous blood) and liver (portal blood) are the commonest sites of haematogenous metastasis - the first capillary bed encountered ("mechanical" theory), plus "seed and soil"

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with a strong family history of breast and ovarian cancer has a BRCAI mutation. Which BRCAI function is disrupted? [KIMS 26]

options.A: Repair of damaged DNA (homologous recombination of

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BRCAI (17q) and BRCA2 (13q) are tumour suppressors for homologous recombination repair; tumours are sensitive to PARP inhibitors (synthetic lethality).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A drug is converted in the liver to a water-soluble conjugate for excretion in bile. Which is a phase11 reaction of xenobiotic metabolism. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phase l (functionalization): oxidation (CYP450), reduction. hydrolysis. Phase11 (conjugation)." glucuronidation, sulfation, acetylation, methylation, glutathione and glycine conjugation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A biochemist lists cellular sources of reactive oxygen species. Which process generates ROS in the endoplasmic reticulum. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ROS sources: mitochondrial ETC leakage (main), CYP450 uncoupling. NADPH oxidase of phagocytes, xanthine oxidase, peroxisomal oxidases, radiation, Fenton reaction (Fe,").

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A biology student explains why fibroblasts stop dividing after -50 divisions. What happens with each DNA replication in somatic cells. [KIMS 26. LHR 25. QIMS 25]

options.B: Telomeres shorten, leading eventually to senescence

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: End-replication problem: the lagging strand cannot be completed at chromosome ends ￿ telomere loss (Hayflick limit) ￿ p53/p21 senescence. Cancer cells reactivate telomerase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A 72-year-old has dry, stiff, thickened, less pliable skin. Which change in collagen explains this. [LHR 25]

options.A: Cross-linking of collagen by advanced glycation end-products (AGES)
options.C: Increased collagen degradation by MMPS only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Non-enzymatic glycation of long-lived proteins ￿ AGES cross-link collagen, reducing elasticity (skin, arteries, lens)," accelerated in diabetes. AGE-RAGE binding increases oxidative stress and inflammation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: Post-mortem of an 80-year-old shows yellow-brown granular pigment in neurons and cardiac muscle. What is this pigment? [LHR 25. QIMS 25]

options.A: Lipofuscin ("wear-and-tear" pigment, marker of cellular aging)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lipofuscin: indigestible residue of lipid peroxidation within lysosomes (residual bodies)." accumulates with age (brown atrophy) and is a marker of free-radical injury/cellular aging.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A man drinks heavily every day. Which hepatic enzyme is mainly responsible for oxidizing ethanol? [LHR 25]

options.C: Alcohol dehydrogenase (with CYP2EI induced in chronic drinkers)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ethanol 4 acetaldehyde (ADH. cytosol, NAD.) 4 acetate (ALDH2, mitochondria). Chronic intake induces CYP2EI (MEOS) 4 tolerance, more ROS and paracetamol toxicity. Disulfiram inhibits ALDH.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies the first-line antioxidant enzyme against superoxide radicals. Which enzyme destroys superoxide. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SOD: 2 0,• + 2H' 4 H,0, + O, (Cu/Zn cytosol. Mn mitochondria); catalase: 2 H,0, ￿ 2 H,0 + O,: glutathione peroxidase (selenium)." H,0, + 2GSH 2H,O + GSSG.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies peroxisomal enzymes. Which enzyme breaks H202 into water and oxygen. [CKMC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Catalase (haem enzyme, peroxisomes) has one of the highest turnover numbers; glutathione peroxidase handles low H,0, concentrations in the cytosol.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student classif ies reactive oxygen species. Which of the following is a ROS but NOT a free radical? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Free radicals have an unpaired electron (O,•~, •OH, NO•). H,0, has none but crosses membranes and forms •OH via the Fenton reaction (Fe"). •OH is the most reactive.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A pharmacology student asks what the cytochrome P450 system does. What is its main function in drug metabolism. [BWP 25]

options.B: Phase l oxidation/hydroxylation (monooxygenase) using NADPH and

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CYP450 monooxygenases (ER. mainly liver): RH + O, + NADPH + H. 4 ROH + H,0 + NADP,; electrons from NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase. Also synthesize steroids, bile acids, vitamin D hydroxylation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: The microsomal cytochrome P450 system requires a phospholipid for electron transfer. Which lipid is a component of the cytochrome P450 system? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Microsomal hydroxylase system: cytochrome P450 + NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase (FAD, FMN) + phosphatidylcholine (needed for electron transfer).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A child in a selenium-deficient region develops cardiomyopathy (Keshan disease). Which enzyme requires selenium. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Glutathione peroxidase contains selenocysteine," deiodinases (T4 4 T3) are also selenoproteins. Catalase is haem-iron," SOD uses Cu/Zn or Mn.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies an enzyme that produces a free radical from L-arginine. Which enzyme is it? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. NOS: L-arginine + O, + NADPH 4 NO• + citrulline (needs FAD, FMN, haem, BH4). eNOS (vasodilation), nNOS (neurotransmission), INOS (macrophage killing).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A man with G6PD deficiency has haemolysis on taking primaquine because glutathione cannot be regenerated. Which coenzyme is required to keep glutathione reduced? [QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glutathione peroxidase oxidizes GSH; glutathione reductase regenerates GSH using NADPH from the HMP shunt (G6PD). G6PD deficiency 4 Heinz bodies, bite cells. haemolysis with oxidant drugs (sulfonamides, primaquine, fava beans). Key note: KIMS 25 source keyed coenzyme Qlo.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A drug undergoes phase I metabolism in the liver. Which reaction is a typical phase I biotransformation? [KIMS 26. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phase l introduces/unmasks a polar group (oxidation, hydroxylation, reduction, hydrolysis) - mainly CYP450: phase11 conjugates (glucuronide. sulfate, acetyl, methyl, glutathione). Key note: KIMS 25 source keyed glucuronidation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A factory worker exposed to benzene develops toxic metabolites and aplastic anaemia. Which enzyme family mediates the initial step of benzene metabolism? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Benzene ￿ benzene oxide/phenol/quinones by CYP2EI ￿ toxic to bone marrow (aplastic anaemia, leukaemia). Phase I can produce more toxic metabolites (bioactivation, e.g. paracetamol 4 NAPQI).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A cell must clear proteins damaged by wear and tear. Which mechanism removes damaged proteins? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Damaged/misfolded proteins are tagged with polyubiquitin and degraded by the 26S proteasome; chaperones (heat shock proteins) refold them. Key note: source keyed DNA mismatch repair, which repairs DNA, not proteins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A man on long-term phenytoin finds other drugs become less effective. Which enzyme system is induced? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inducers." phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenobarbital, chronic alcohol, St John's wort, smoking. Inhibitors: cimetidine, ketoconazole, erythromycin, grapefruit juice, isoniazid.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A pharmacology student asks how many lipid-soluble drugs are detoxified in the liver. By which reaction do cytochrome P450 enzymes primarily act? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CYP450 monooxygenases insert one O atom into the substrate (RH 4 ROH) and reduce the other to water; the products are then conjugated (phase

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A woman on rifampicin for TB becomes pregnant despite taking oral contraceptives. By which mechanism does rifampicin reduce OCP efficacy. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Enzyme induction increases metabolism of estrogen and progestogen 4 lower levels; use additional contraception or an IUD.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student explains the purpose of drug conjugation reactions. Phase11 reactions convert lipid-soluble compounds into what? [CKMC 26]

options.A: Water-soluble conjugates for excretion in urine or bile

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Conjugation with glucuronic acid (UDP-glucuronyl transferase), sulfate (PAPS), glutathione. acetyl-CoA, glycine or SAM increases polarity and molecular weight, aiding renal and biliary excretion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: In cells deprived of f ibroblast growth factor stimulation, proliferation slows. Which activity may decline in such cells. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Growth factors (FGF, EGF) induce TER T expression and telomerase activity in proliferating cells; reduced stimulation lowers telomerase, favouring telomere shortening and senescence. Source stem was weak/reconstructed.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A patient with mitochondrial myopathy has damaged respiratory chain complexes. What can mitochondrial dysfunction lead to. [CKMC 26. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Damaged ETC complexes leak more electrons 4 superoxide ￿ mtDNA and lipid damage (vicious cycle); ATP falls and lactate rises. Central to the mitochondrial theory of aging.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: After paracetamol overdose, the toxic metabolite NAPQI is detoxified by conjugation with glutathione. Which functional group of glutathione reacts directly. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glutathione = y-glutamyl-cysteinyl-glycine," its cysteine thiol conjugates electrophiles (GST) and reduces peroxides. When GSH is depleted, NAPQI binds liver proteins 4 centrilobular necrosis: N-acetylcysteine replenishes GSH.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A smoker with a reduced-function CYP2A6 variant needs fewer cigarettes for the same nicotine effect. Which finding explains this? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CYP2A6 converts nicotine to cotinine; slow metabolizers keep higher nicotine levels - an example of pharmacogenetic polymorphism (others: CYP2D6, CYP2C19, NAT2 slow acetylators).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A cell accumulates superoxide and hydrogen peroxide under oxidative stress. Which antioxidant enryme combination most directly removes both? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SOD converts O,•- ￿ H,0,; glutathione peroxidase (Se) or catalase converts H,0, ￿ H,0. Glutathione reductase regenerates GSH (NADPH) but does not remove ROS itself.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: Stem created: the HITEC item was cropped (options B-D: impaired brain glucose metabolism, F-amyloid, reduced neurotransmitters). A 75-year-old with progressive memory loss is studied for age-related neurodegeneration. Which finding is the hallmark protein abnormality of Alzheimer disease? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Impaired glucose metabolism in the brain

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alzheimer: extracellular F-amyloid plaques (APP cleavage), intracellular tau tangles, cholinergic loss," oxidative stress and reduced cerebral glucose use (seen on FDG-PET) are secondary features.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A 12-year-old has premature greying, cataracts and skin atrophy; testing shows a defect in maintaining chromosome-end stability during replication. Which condition best explains this? [HITEC 26]

options.D: Telomere shortening leading to early cellular senescence

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Premature aging syndromes: Werner (WRN helicase, adult onset), Hutchinson-Gilford progeria (lamin A), dyskeratosis congenita (telomerase). Short telomeres trigger p53-mediated senescence.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student studies cellular self-eating that clears damaged organelles and declines with age. Which organelle is most closely linked to autophagy. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Autophagosomes fuse with lysosomes for degradation; impaired autophagy with age leads to accumulation of damaged proteins/organelles and lipofuscin. Caloric restriction enhances autophagy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A patient on isoniazid for TB develops peripheral neuropathy; he is a slow acetylator. By which reaction is isoniazid mainly detoxified? [HITEC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NAT2 polymorphism: slow acetylators (~50% of South Asians) get isoniazid neuropathy (give pyridoxine), hydralazine/procainamide drug-induced lupus," fast acetylators risk hepatotoxicity.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student studies the microsomal hydroxylating system. Which coenzyme is required by cytochrome P450 reductase. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase (FAD and FMN) transfers two electrons from NADPH one at a time to the haem of P450. Mitochondrial P450s (steroidogenesis) use adrenodoxin and adrenodoxin reductase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A drug inhibits glucose~6~phosphate dehydrogenase, reducing NADPH production. Which process is impaired most directly. [BWP 26]

options.D: Reductive biosynthesis and maintenance of reduced glutathione

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NADPH (HMP shunt)." fatty acid, cholesterol and steroid synthesis, glutathione reductase, CYP450 reductase, NADPH oxidase (respiratory burst), NOS.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A gerontologist explains why cells deteriorate with age. What does the free-radical theory of aging propose. [BWP 26]

options.A: Aging results from increased protein synthesis
options.B: Aging results from accumulated oxidative damage by free radicals
options.C: Aging results from reduced DNA methylation alone

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Harman free-radical theory: ROS damage to DNA (esp. mtDNA), proteins (carbonylation) and lipids accumulates; supported by links between metabolic rate, antioxidant capacity and lifespan.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student studies phase11 conjugation of steroids and phenols. PAPS donates a sulfate group in which reaction. [BWP 261
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Donors: PAPS (sulfate), UDP-glucuronic acid (glucuronide), acetyl-CoA (acetyl), SAM (methyl), GSH (glutathione).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student studies replicative lifespan. Which enzyme helps delay replicative senescence. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Telomerase (TERT reverse transcriptase + TERC RNA template) adds TTAGGG repeats,. active in germ cells, stem cells and~90A of cancers; most somatic cells lack it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A student studies antioxidants that act in cell membranes. Which antioxidant primarily protects membranes by breaking lipid peroxidation chains. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitamin E (lipid-soluble, chain-breaking) traps peroxyl radicals in membranes," vitamin C (water-soluble) regenerates it,. deficiency ￿ haemolysis, spinocerebellar ataxia, peripheral neuropathy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.topicName: Molecular Insights - Aging, Free Radicals & Xenobiotics
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old has mild jaundice after fasting, with raised unconjugated bilirubin and normal liver enzymes. Which reaction is affected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gilbert syndrome: reduced UGTIAI activity (promoter TA repeat) ￿ mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with stress/fasting. Crigler-Najjar: absent (l) or severe (11) deficiency. Key note: source stem called it phase l - glucuronidation is phase11.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist measures the main cellular source of superoxide anion. During which process is superoxide mainly generated? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]

options.C: Oxidative phosphorylation (electron leakage at complexes l and111)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. About 1-2% of electrons leak from the ETC to O, forming O,• , removed by Mn-SOD in mitochondria. Increased ROS production contributes to aging (free radical theory).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares ATP yields from glucose. What is the approximate ATP yield from anaerobic glycolysis versus complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anaerobic glycolysis: net 2 ATP (4 made - 2 used). Aerobic." _30-32 ATP (modern P/0 ratios: NADH 2.5, FADH, 1.5)," older texts give 36-38.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher adds oligomycin to isolated mitochondria; oxygen consumption falls. Which component does oligomycin inhibit? [AMC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oligomycin blocks the Fo proton channel 4 protons cannot re-enter 4 gradient builds up and electron flow stops (respiratory control). Uncouplers (DNP) restore O, use without ATP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A fire victim has severe lactic acidosis and bright red venous blood. Which complex does cyanide inhibit? [AMC 26]

options.C: Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase, Fe" of haem a))

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Complex IV inhibitors: cyanide, carbon monoxide, azide, H,S. Complex I: rotenone, amytal; Complex111: antimycin A.. Complex V." oligomycin. Treat cyanide with hydroxocobalamin or nitrites + thiosulfate.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newborn keeps warm without shivering. Which protein is responsible for non-shivering thermogenesis in brown fat? [AMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UCPI lets protons leak back into the matrix, dissipating the gradient as heat (physiological uncoupling); activated by NE via F3 receptors and free fatty acids.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student draws the electron transport chain. Which complexes pump protons into the intermembrane space. [CKMC 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Complex l (4 H.), 111 (4 H., Q cycle), IV (2 H,) pump protons," Complex11 (succinate dehydrogenase) does not - so FADH2 yields less ATP (1.5) than NADH (2.5).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: NADH is produced when malate is oxidized in the TCA cycle. To which complex does this NADH donate electrons? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NADH ￿ Complex l (FMN, Fe-s) ￿ COQ," FADH, from succinate ￿ Complex11￿ COQ; glycerol-3-phosphate and fatty acyl-CoA dehydrogenases also feed COQ via FAD.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher adds antimycin A, a Complex111 inhibitor, to respiring mitochondria. What is the redox state of carriers before and after the block? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Carriers upstream of a block (NADH, COQ) accumulate electrons and become fully reduced," carriers downstream (cyt c, a, a3) give up electrons to O, and become oxidized.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man taking a slimming" drug has hyperthermia; ATP synthesis falls while 02 consumption rises. What is the cause. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uncouplers (DNP, high-dose aspirin, thermogenin) carry protons across the inner membrane bypassing ATP synthase ￿ electron transport speeds up, energy lost as heat. Inhibitors reduce 02 use.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces electrons through the respiratory chain. Which complex transfers electrons to oxygen. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Complex IV (cyt a, a,, CUA, CUB) reduces O, to 2 H,0 using four electrons from cytochrome c; O, is the final electron acceptor.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies the structure of ATP synthase; oligomycin binds the Fo portion. Which component contains the catalytic sites for ATP synthesis? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: F. (membrane, proton channel - "O" for oligomycin) rotates the y stalk; F, (a3F3 head) synthesizes ATP by the binding-change mechanism (Boyer). -3 H" per ATP plus I for transport.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Oligomycin is added to respiring mitochondria. Which combination of changes is most likely. [MUL 26]

options.A: T ATP, t gradient, l O, consumption
options.B: I ATP, I gradient, t O, consumption
options.C: t ATP, I gradient, t O, consumption
options.D: I ATP synthesis, t proton gradient, l oxygen consumption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Blocking ATP synthase builds up the proton gradient until it prevents further pumping ￿ electron flow and 02 use fall (respiratory control). Adding an uncoupler then restores 02 use without ATP (option B pattern = uncoupling).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A young man has painless bilateral visual loss from Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, a mitochondrial mutation reducing Complex l activity. Which function is most directly affected? [MUL 26. BWP 26. KIMS 26]

options.A: Transfer of electrons from NADH to ubiquinone
options.B: Transfer from cytochrome c to O,
options.D: Transfer from ubiquinone to cytochrome c

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LHON." mtDNA mutations in ND genes (complex l), maternal inheritance, young males. Rotenone and amytal also block complex I; FADH,-linked substrates (succinate) bypass it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane, which is impermeable to most charged molecules. Which pair is transported by a specif ic transport protein. [MUL 26]

options.B: ATP and ADP (adenine nucleotide translocase, antiport)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ANT exchanges matrix ATP for cytosolic ADP (inhibited by atractyloside. bongkrekic acid)," phosphate enters with H.. NADH cannot cross - reducing equivalents enter via the malate-aspartate and glycerol-phosphate shuttles.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student locates the respiratory chain in mitochondria. Where is the electron transport chain located? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inner membrane: Etc complexes, ATP synthase, ANT, cardiolipin." impermeable to H.. Matrix: TCA cycle (except succinate dehydrogenase. an inner-membrane enzyme = complex11), F-oxidation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains chemiosmosis. What is the principal purpose of the electrochemical gradient generated by the ETC? [HITEC 26]

options.A: To create a pore in the inner membrane
options.B: To generate substrates for ATP synthesis
options.C: To drive conformational changes in ATP synthase that form ATP

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mitchell chemiosmotic theory: proton-motive force (ApH + membrane potential) drives protons through F,, rotating the y subunit and causing binding-change conformations in F, F subunits.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A reaction in the cell has a positive standard f ree-energy change. How can such a reaction be made to proceed? [HITEC 26]

options.D: Coupling with ATP hydrolysis (an exergonic reaction)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Free energies are additive: coupling an endergonic reaction to ATP hydrolysis (AG°_ _7.3 kcal/mol) through a common intermediate makes the overall AG negative. Enzymes change rate. not AG.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies how cytosolic NADH reducing equivalents enter mitochondria in heart and liver. How does malate cross the inner mitochondrial membrane in the malate-aspartate shuttle. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Malate-aspartate shuttle (liver, heart, kidney) 4 NADH in matrix (2.5 ATP); glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle (muscle, brain) 4 FADH, (1.5 ATP).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A bodybuilder uses an illegal slimming drug and develops fatal hyperthermia. Which of the following is an uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uncouplers (DNP, high-dose salicylates, dicoumarol, thermogenin) are lipophilic weak acids that ferry H" across the inner membrane 4 t O, use, I ATP, heat.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A reaction has a positive ￿G. yet proceeds in the cell. Which statement explains this. [KIMS 26]

options.A: A positive ￿G. means the reaction can never occur
options.B: Actual AG depends on the concentrations of reactants and products
options.D: ￿G. becomes negative when ATP is present

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AG = AG. + RT In([products]/[reactants]),. keeping products low (removal by the next enzyme) or substrates high makes AG negative (e.g. aldolase, triose phosphate isomerase).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After exposure to fumes in a closed room, a man has headache, confusion, hypotension, lactic acidosis and cherry-red skin. Which electron transport chain complex is affected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin (carboxy-Hb, cherry-red) and cytochrome c oxidase; cyanide also inhibits complex IV. Treat CO with lOO% O, or hyperbaric oxygen. ENDOCRINOLOGY - INTRODUCTION (HORMONES & MECHANISMS OF ACTION)

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with hypoglycaemia is given glucagon. Which hormone acts by increasing CAMP formation. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CAMP hormones (Gs): glucagon, ACTH, TSH, LH. FSH, PTH, calcitonin, ADH (V2), F-adrenergic. Insulin and IGF-I 4 tyrosine kinase; GH, prolactin JAK-STAT," thyroid/steroids 4 nuclear receptors.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares the plasma half-lives of glycoprotein hormones; more sialic acid prolongs half-life. Which order (longest to shortest) is correct? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: hCG F-subunit has a C-terminal peptide rich in sialylated O-glycans ￿ half-life -24-36 h; FSH (-3-4 h) > TSH/LH (~1 h, less sialic acid).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After insulin binds its receptor, GLUT-4 moves to the muscle cell membrane. Which pathway mediates GLUT-4 translocation. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Insulin receptor (tyrosine kinase) 4 IRS-I 4 P13K 4 PIP3 4 Akt (PKB) 4 GLUT4 translocation, glycogen synthesis; Ras-MAPK mediates growth/mitogenic effects.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Glucagon binds its receptor on a hepatocyte. What is the first intracellular event? [BWP 26. KIMS 26. QIMS 25]

options.D: Activation of the G-protein (Gs, GDP4GTP exchange)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied.. the source gave no answer key. Sequence: hormone-GPCR binding 4 Gsa exchanges GDP for GTP 4 adenylyl cyclase 4 CAMP 4 PKA phosphorylation cascade (glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with hypothyroidism has a raised TSH. Which second messenger pathway does TSH activate in thyroid cells? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. TSH receptor (Gs, and Gq at high levels) ￿ CAMP ￿ PKA ￿ iodide uptake (NIS), thyroglobulin synthesis, TPO activity. hormone release and follicular cell growth.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies oxytocin receptors in the myometrium. Through which mechanism does oxytocin act? [CKMC 26]

options.D: Gq - phospholipase C - IPJDAG ( t intracellular Ca")

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IPJDAG hormones: oxytocin, ADH (VI), TRH, GnRH, angiotensin11, al-adrenergic, gastrin. ADH V2 receptors in the kidney use CAMP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hormone binds a cell-surface receptor lacking intrinsic kinase activity and activates associated tyrosine kinases that regulate gene transcription. Which hormone uses this pathway. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cytokine-receptor family (JAK-STA T): GH, prolactin, leptin, erythropoietin, interleukins. Insulin/lGF-I receptors have intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity; glucagon uses GS-CAMP; cortisol uses intracellular receptors.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies glucocorticoid action on gene expression. Which statement best describes glucocorticoid receptor-mediated gene regulation. [MUL 26]

options.A: The free lipophilic hormone diffuses across the membrane and binds
options.B: The receptor is located only on the cell membrane a cytoplasmic receptor, which moves to the nucleus
options.D: The hormone-receptor complex binds directly to ribosomes

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucocorticoid receptor (cytoplasmic, bound to HSP90) ￿ hormone binding releases HSP90 ￿ dimer enters nucleus ￿ binds glucocorticoid response elements (GRE) 4 transcription. Thyroid hormone receptors are already nuclear.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with type 2 diabetes has impaired insulin signalling in skeletal muscle. Which molecular event initiates signalling after insulin binds its receptor. [MUL 26]

options.A: Autophosphorylation of tyrosine residues on the receptor F~subunits
options.D: Opening of a ligand-gated ion channel

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin receptor." a2F2 tetramer; insulin binds the extracellular a-subunits 4 F-subunit tyrosine kinase autophosphorylates 4 phosphorylates IRS-I P13K/Akt (metabolic) and Ras/MAPK (growth).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares plasma half-lives of hormones. Which hormone has the shortest plasma half-life. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Catecholamines: half-life 1-3 minutes (reuptake, COMT, MAO). Steroids." minutes to -1-2 h (protein-bound); T4: _7 days (TBG-bound), T3: _ 1 day.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student draws the insulin receptor. Which subunit lies outside the cell and binds insulin. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: a subunits." extracellular insulin-binding," F subunits: transmembrane with cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase; linked by disulfide bonds (a2F2). Mutations leprechaunism, type A insulin resistance.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with erythema infectiosum has "slapped cheeks" and a lacy rash from local vasodilation. To which class do the vasodilator chemical messengers (prostaglandins) belong. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Eicosanoids (prostaglandins, prostacyclin, thromboxanes, leukotrienes) are local autocrine/paracrine mediators made from arachidonic acid; PGE2/PG12 cause vasodilation. Messenger in the source was unspecified.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with asthma is given montelukast. From which precursor are leukotrienes derived? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Membrane phospholipids ￿ phospholipase A2 (inhibited by steroids) 4 arachidonic acid ￿ COX (prostaglandins, thromboxanes," inhibited by NSAIDS) or 5-LOX (leukotrienes; zileuton).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student defines types of chemical signalling. An endocrine hormone is best defined as a messenger that: [BWP 26]

options.A: Acts only on the secreting cell
options.C: Acts only within the cell that makes it
options.D: Is secreted into the bloodstream and acts on distant target cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endocrine (blood-borne, distant)," paracrine (neighbouring cells, e.g. somatostatin in islets); autocrine (same cell, e.g. IL-2 on T cells)," neurocrine (synaptic). ENDOCRINOLOGY- HYPOTHALAMUS & PITUITARY

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists anterior pituitary hormones that act on other endocrine glands. Which is a tropic hormone released from the anterior pituitary. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Tropic hormones stimulate other glands: TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH (and GH via IGF-I). Prolactin acts directly on the breast; oxytocin and ADH are posterior pituitary hormones.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has high growth hormone and high IGF-I levels with normal pituitary imaging; a pancreatic tumour is found. What is the cause of acromegaly here. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Most acromegaly is from a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma; rarely ectopic GHRH (pancreatic/carcinoid tumours) causes somatotroph hyperplasia. IGF-I is the best screening test; OGTT fails to suppress GH.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient has high ACTH and high cortisol due to a hypothalamic tumour. What is the primary hormonal abnormality. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CRH (hypothalamus) 4 ACTH (anterior pituitary) 4 cortisol; cortisol inhibits both CRH and ACTH (negative feedback). Primary adrenal disease: cortisol t, ACTH I .

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A night-shift worker has disturbed sleep. A pineal hormone normally rises at night. Which hormone from pinealocytes is secreted at night? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Darkness 4 SCN 4 sympathetic (superior cervical ganglion) ￿ pinealocytes N-acetyltransferase t ￿ melatonin (from serotonin). Melatonin regulates circadian rhythm and inhibits GnRH.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with absent puberty also cannot smell (anosmia). Which hypothalamic hormone deficiency causes Kallmann syndrome. [QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Kallmann: failed migration of GnRH neurons from the olfactory placode (KALI/ANOSI) 4 hypogonadotropic hypogonadism + anosmia. Low FSH/LH, low sex steroids.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has an enlarged jaw, deep voice, increasing ring size and headaches. Which raised hormone mediates the facial and acral growth? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Acromegaly." GH-secreting adenoma 4 IGF-I ￿ soft-tissue and bone overgrowth, insulin resistance, cardiomyopathy. Screen with IGF-I; confirm by failure of GH suppression after OGTh.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies hypothalamic control of reproduction. Which hypothalamic hormone controls FSH and LH release? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pulsatile GnRH (every 60-90 min) stimulates FSH/LH; continuous GnRH agonist (leuprolide) downregulates receptors - used in prostate cancer, endometriosis. precocious puberty.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies the stress response. Which hypothalamic hormone initiates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CRH (paraventricular nucleus, with ADH synergy) 4 ACTH (POMC cleavage) 4 cortisol. Circadian peak in the early morning," stress overrides feedback.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student classifies hypothalamic control of anterior pituitary hormones. Which hormone is controlled predominantly by a hypothalamic inhibiting hormone (dopamine)? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dopamine (PIH) from the arcuate nucleus via the tuberoinfundibular pathway tonically inhibits lactotrophs," antipsychotics (D2 blockers) and stalk lesions raise prolactin." bromocriptine/cabergoline lower it. ENDOCRINOLOGY - THYROID

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies the protein in thyroid follicles on which hormones are built. Which amino acid of thyroglobulin is iodinated to form thyroid hormones? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroglobulin (~660 kDa glycoprotein) has- 120 tyrosines; TPO iodinates them (MIT, DIT) and couples DIT+DIT ￿ T4, MIT+DIT 4 T3.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with fatigue has low T4 and high TSH. Which thyroid enzyme catalyses both iodide oxidation and iodination of tyrosine residues. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. TPO (on the apical membrane, uses H,0, from DUOX) - oxidation, organification and coupling; inhibited by carbimazole/PTU." anti-TPO antibodies in Hashimoto disease.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with heat intolerance and weight loss has a goitre. How does thyroid hormone act at the molecular level? [CKMC 26. MUL 26. KIMS 26. QIMS 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: transcription / Exam Pearl: T3 binds nuclear thyroid hormone receptors (TRa/F) heterodimerized with RXR on thyroid response elements 4 transcription of Na'/K'_ATPase, -receptors, mitochondrial enzymes, myosin.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient has normal T4, low T3 and raised reverse T3 during severe illness. Which enzyme activity is reduced? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sick euthyroid (low T3) syndrome." fasting, illness, glucocorticoids, propranolol, amiodarone and PTU reduce type 1/2 5-deiodinase (T4 4 T3): inner-ring (type 3) deiodination makes reverse T3.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman has a raised total T4 but normal free T4. Which plasma protein carries the largest proportion of thyroxine? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TBG carries ~70AO . transthyretin -10- 15¥0. albumin ~15-20%; only 0.03AO of T4 is free. Estrogen (pregnancy, OCP) raises TBG; androgens and nephrotic syndrome lower it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with thyroid storm is given a drug that blocks iodide uptake. Which drug inhibits iodide trapping by the thyroid? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Iodide is trapped by the Na'/l- symporter (NIS) using the Na. gradient; perchlorate, pertechnetate and thiocyanate compete with iodide. Thionamides (carbimazole, PTU) block TPO; PTU also blocks peripheral deiodination.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Thyroid tests show low T3n4 and high TSH. What do these results indicate. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary (thyroid) failure: low T4, high TSH (most common." Hashimoto, iodine deficiency). Secondary (pituitary): low T4 with low/normal TSH. Subclinical.. high TSH, normal T4.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with severe iodine deficiency has reduced thyroid hormone synthesis. Which process is responsible for the initial uptake of iodide. [MUL 26]

options.B: Active transport of iodide into follicular cells by the Na'/l- symporter

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NIS (basolateral, secondary active, driven by Na'/K'_ATPase) concentrates iodide 20-40x; pendrin moves it into colloid. TSH increases NIS. Perchlorate and thiocyanate block NIS.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies peripheral thyroid hormone activation. Which enzyme is primarily responsible for peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 in liver and kidney. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DI (liver, kidney, thyroid; PTU-sensitive) supplies plasma T3; D2 (brain, pituitary, muscle, brown fat) supplies intracellular T3; D3 inactivates (T4 - rT3, T3 ￿ T2). All are selenoproteins. ENDOCRINOLOGY- PARATHYROID & CALCIUM HOMEOSTASIS

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with hypocalcaemia has normal PTH receptors. By which second messenger does PTH act on its target cells. [Prof 24. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PTH receptor (PTHIR) is Gs-coupled 4 c4MP (urinary CAMP rises; absent in pseudohypoparathyroidism, Gsa mutation). It also activates Gq-PLC.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with chronic kidney disease has a low serum bicarbonate. Why does chronic kidney disease cause metabolic acidosis. [AMC 25]

options.C: Reduced renal H. excretion and ammonium (NH,.) production

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Source stem said "metabolic alkalosis"; CKD causes metabolic ACIDOSIS. CKD also gives hypocalcaemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism from reduced la-hydroxylation of vitamin D and phosphate retention.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old with poor sun exposure has bowed legs, rachitic rosary and wide wrists. What is this condition. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitamin D deficiency before epiphyseal closure ￿ rickets (defective mineralization of growth plate); after closure ￿ osteomalacia. Labs: l /normal Ca, I phosphate, t ALP, t PTH.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies regulation of osteoclasts. Which hormone increases osteoprotegerin (OPG) and so reduces osteoclastic activity. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: OPG is a decoy receptor for RANKL; estrogen t OPG and l RANKL. Calcitonin inhibits osteoclasts directly via its receptor. PTH and cortisol favour corrected. resorption. Source stem said "inhibit OPG"

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man has bone pain, enlarging skull and very high alkaline phosphatase (Paget disease). Which hormone can be given to reduce osteoclastic activity. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Paget disease: excessive disorganized osteoclastic then osteoblastic activity ￿ mosaic bone, t ALP, normal Ca. Calcitonin binds osteoclast receptors and inhibits resorption.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with chronic kidney disease has perioral tingling and serum calcium of 7.2 mg/dL. Which mechanism causes hypocalcaemia. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. CKD: I la-hydroxylase and phosphate retention ￿ hypocalcaemia ￿ secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal osteodystrophy. Treat with calcitriol and phosphate binders.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has bone pain, kidney stones, hypercalcaemia and low phosphate. How does the raised hormone cause hypercalcaemia. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]

options.B: Increased osteoclast activity (via RANKL from osteoblasts)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Primary hyperparathyroidism ("stones. bones, groans. moans"): PTH t bone resorption, t renal Ca reabsorption, I phosphate reabsorption, t calcitriol. PTH acts on osteoblasts, which signal osteoclasts.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Within minutes of PTH secretion, calcium handling changes. Which organ is the main immediate target of PTH'S rapid effects. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PTH: rapid - t distal tubular Ca" reabsorption. I proximal phosphate reabsorption (phosphaturia), osteocytic osteolysis: slower - osteoclastic resorption and t la-hydroxylase (intestinal absorption via calcitriol).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has bowed legs despite adequate dietary vitamin D; phosphate is low and urinary phosphate high. What is the likely condition. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: X-linked hypophosphataemic rickets: PHEX mutation ￿ t FGF23 ￿ renal phosphate wasting and low calcitriol," calcium and PTH near normal. Treat with phosphate + calcitriol (or burosumab).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man on haemodialysis has very high PTH, low calcium and high phosphate. What is the primary cause of secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD? [LHR 26. KIMS 26]

options.B: Phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol production

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phosphate retention ( t FGF23) and I la-hydroxylase 4 hypocalcaemia 4 parathyroid hyperplasia; long-standing disease may become autonomous (tertiary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcaemia).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists renal actions of hormones. Which hormone increases renal calcium reabsorption and causes phosphaturia. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PTH.. t Ca" reabsorption in the distal tubule, I phosphate reabsorption in the proximal tubule (internalizes NaPi-Ila), t la-hydroxylase. FGF23 also causes phosphaturia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A young woman has cramps and perioral tingling without neck surgery; she is short with short 4th metacarpals. Which laboratory profile fits pseudohypoparathyroidism. [MUL 26]

options.B: tCa" IPTH I po,, t PTH, t ALP I po,,

mcqs.explanation: tPTH/ t PO,, t PO,, Exam Pearl: End-organ resistance to PTH (GSLVGNAS mutation, Albright hereditary osteodystrophy) 4 hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia despite HIGH PTH," no rise in urinary CAMP after PTH. Vitamin D deficiency gives low phosphate.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with flank pain has hypercalcaemia, hypophosphataemia and markedly raised PTH. Which kidney enzyme does PTH activate. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitamin D: skin 7-dehydrocholesterol ￿ D3 ￿ liver 25-hydroxylase 4 25(OH)D 4 kidney la-hydroxylase ( t by PTH, low phosphate; I by FGF23) 1,25(OH),D. 24-hydroxylase makes inactive 24,25(OH),D.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman develops tetany a week after thyroidectomy. What is the commonest cause of primary hypoparathyroidism. [BWP 26]

options.A: Destruction or removal of the parathyroid glands (surgical)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Causes: post-surgical (thyroid/parathyroid/neck surgery) > autoimmune (APS-I), DiGeorge, hypomagnesaemia (functional), infiltration. ENDOCRINOLOGY- ADRENAL GLAND

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with phaeochromocytoma has high adrenal medullary hormones. What is the chemical nature of adrenal medullary hormones? [AMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Classes: amino acid-derived (catecholamines, thyroid hormones, melatonin), peptides/proteins (insulin, GH), glycoproteins (TSH, FSH. LH, hCG), steroids (cortisol, aldosterone, sex steroids, calcitriol).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces adrenaline synthesis in the adrenal medulla. Which enzyme converts norepinephrine to epinephrine? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PNMT uses SAM as methyl donor and is induced by cortisol carried in the intra-adrenal portal blood - hence adrenaline is made mainly in the adrenal medulla.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has central obesity, purple striae and proximal myopathy. Plasma ACTH is high and cortisol is suppressed only by high-dose dexamethasone. What is the cause. [MUL 26. LHR 25]

options.A: Ectopic ACTH from small-cell lung cancer

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High-dose dexamethasone suppresses pituitary (but not ectopic) ACTH; adrenal tumours have low ACTH. Commonest cause of Cushing syndrome overall is exogenous glucocorticoids.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man on high-dose steroids develops adrenal changes; a student asks where cortisol is made. Which adrenal zone secretes cortisol? [WMC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "Salt, sugar, sex - the deeper you go the sweeter it gets": glomerulosa (aldosterone), fasciculata (cortisol), reticularis (androgens). Fasciculata is the widest zone.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
