mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman has episodic headache, palpitations and sweating; imaging shows an adrenal medullary tumour. What is the diagnosis. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Phaeochromocytoma: catecholamine excess (paroxysmal hypertension, the triad of headache, sweating, palpitations); t urinary VMA/metanephrines; associated with MEN 2, VHL. NFI.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In a patient with renal artery stenosis, angiotensin11 rises. On which part of the adrenal does angiotensin11 act to increase aldosterone? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Aldosterone regulators: angiotensin 11 and plasma K. (most important), ACTH (minor, permissive). Aldosterone synthase (CYPIIB2) is unique to the glomerulosa.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies adrenal steroid synthesis. Which enzyme catalyses the rate-limiting step. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Cholesterol 4 pregnenolone in mitochondria (StAR protein transports cholesterol in; ACTH stimulates). Congenital lipoid adrenal hyperplasia = StAR defect.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 3-day-old has vomiting, dehydration, hypotension and ambiguous genitalia. Which pattern suggests 21-hydroxylase deficiency. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Decreased aldosterone and cortisol, increased androgens
options.B: Decreased cortisol, increased aldosterone and androgens

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. 21-OH deficiency (90% of CAH): no cortisol/aldosterone 4 salt wasting. hyperkalaemia," precursors diverted to androgens ￿ virilization of females," t 17-hydroxyprogesterone.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has purple abdominal striae, moon face and proximal muscle weakness. These features are characteristic of which condition. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortisol excess breaks down dermal collagen (thin skin, wide purple striae, bruising), causes central obesity, hypertension, hyperglycaemia, osteoporosis and myopathy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has fatigue, hypotension, hyperpigmentation, low cortisol and high ACTH. What is the diagnosis. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Addison: adrenal destruction (autoimmune, TB) 4 I cortisol and aldosterone 4 hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypotension; t ACTH/POMC MSH-like hyperpigmentation (absent in secondary insufficiency).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has primary adrenal insufficiency from autoimmune adrenalitis. Which hormones are deficient in primary Addison disease. [WMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary failure affects all cortical zones 4 glucocorticoid + mineralocorticoid (+ adrenal androgen) deficiency; medulla is usually spared. Secondary (pituitary) failure spares aldosterone.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists the major actions of excess cortisol in Cushing syndrome. Which group is correct? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Reduced gluconeogenesis, increased protein synthesis, hypotension
options.C: Increased gluconeogenesis, protein catabolism and vascular

mcqs.explanation: responsiveness to catecholamines / Exam Pearl: Cortisol." gluconeogenesis, insulin resistance, protein breakdown (thin skin, myopathy), fat redistribution, permissive action on catecholamines (hypertension), immunosuppression, bone loss.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with primary adrenal insufficiency becomes hypoglycaemic after missing meals. What does cortisol deficiency most directly cause. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Increased ability to maintain fasting glucose
options.B: Decreased ability to maintain fasting glucose

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortisol is needed for gluconeogenic enzyme induction (PEPCK, G-6-Pase) and for permissive action of glucagon and adrenaline," Addison patients are prone to fasting hypoglycaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with Addison disease has hyperpigmentation of the palmar creases and buccal mucosa. What is it primarily due to. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of cortisol feedback 4 t POMC 4 ACTH and a-MSH stimulate melanocortin-l receptors on melanocytes. Pituitary ACTH tumours (Cushing disease. Nelson syndrome after adrenalectomy) also cause pigmentation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman on long-term prednisolone develops vertebral fractures. How do glucocorticoids decrease bone mass? [BWP 26]

options.B: Inhibit bone formation and increase bone resorption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucocorticoids: l osteoblast function and lifespan (main effect), t RANKL/I OPG, l intestinal Ca absorption, t urinary Ca loss. I sex steroids.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man has a 24-hour urine test showing markedly increased vanillylmandelic acid. What does this suggest? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VMA and metanephrines are catecholamine metabolites (MAO + COMT)," plasma free metanephrines are the most sensitive test. HVA (dopamine metabolite) is raised in neuroblastoma.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies aldosterone action on the collecting duct principal cells. What is the effect of aldosterone on the distal nephron. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Increased Na. reabsorption and K, (and H") secretion
options.C: Decreased Na, reabsorption and K, secretion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid receptor) 4 t ENaC, Na'/K'_ATPase and ROMK in principal cells,. t H'_ATPase in intercalated cells. Spironolactone blocks the receptor; amiloride blocks ENaC. ENDOCRINOLOGY- ENDOCRINE PANCREAS

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic wants to know how well his glucose was controlled over the last 3 months. Which is the best test? [Prof 24. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HbAlc (non-enzymatic glycation of HbA F-chain N-terminal valine) reflects mean glucose over-8-12 weeks (RBC lifespan). >6.5% is diagnostic of diabetes,. target <7% in most diabetics.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with type 2 diabetes starts metformin. An oral antihyperglycaemic drug primarily lowers the level of which substance? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Metformin I hepatic gluconeogenesis (AMPK) and improves insulin sensitivity without causing hypoglycaemia; sulfonylureas increase insulin release.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old obese man has type 2 diabetes with high insulin levels. To which hormone do the target tissues show resistance. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Type 2 DM: insulin resistance (post-receptor defects, obesity, inflammation) with relative F-cell failure; type I: autoimmune F-cell destruction (absolute deficiency).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a meal, insulin promotes glycogen storage in liver and muscle. How does insulin act on glycogen synthase. [AMC 25]

options.D: Activates it by dephosphorylation (protein phosphatase-l, inhibition

mcqs.explanation: of GSK-3) 1 Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Insulin 4 P13K 4 Akt inhibits GSK-3 and activates PP-I 4 dephosphorylated (active) glycogen synthase and inactive glycogen phosphorylase. Glucagon/adrenaline ￿ PKA ￿ phosphorylation (opposite).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After oral glucose, more insulin is released than after the same amount of IV glucose. Which hormone enhances insulin secretion in this incretin effect? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Incretins from L-cells (GLP-I) and K-cells (GIP) potentiate glucose-dependent insulin secretion." GLP-I analogues (liraglutide) and DPP-4 inhibitors (sitagliptin) are used in type 2 diabetes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with coeliac disease develops polyuria and hyperglycaemia. Which type of diabetes is associated with coeliac disease. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options created: the source recalled only the stem and answer. Type l DM and coeliac disease share HLA-DQ2/DQ8 and autoimmunity," screen TIDM children for coeliac disease (anti-tTG antibodies).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old with renal failure and K" 7 mmol/L is given IV insulin with glucose. What is the effect of insulin here. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin and F2 agonists drive K. into cells." calcium gluconate stabilizes the myocardium; resins/dialysis remove K.. Glucose prevents hypoglycaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a meal, insulin lowers blood glucose partly by changing hepatic enzyme levels. Which enzyme does insulin induce in the liver. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin induces glucokinase. PFK-I (via F-2,6-BP), pyruvate kinase, glycogen synthase; represses gluconeogenic enzymes (pyruvate carboxylase. PEPCK, F-1,6-BPase, G-6-Pase) and increases GLUT4 in muscle/fat.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares glucose transporters. Which transporter is insulin-dependent in muscle and adipose tissue? [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. GLUTI: RBC, brain, BBB; GLUT2: liver, F-cells, intestine/kidney basolateral (high Km); GLUT3: neurons; GLUT4: muscle, fat (insulin-regulated); GLUT5: fructose.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cell biologist traces insulin synthesis in F-cells. In which organelle is preproinsulin synthesized? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Preproinsulin (RER," signal peptide removed) 4 proinsulin 4 Golgi/secretory granules where prohormone convertases cleave C-peptide ￿ insulin (A and B chains with 2 disulfide bridges) + C-peptide in equimolar amounts.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic on insulin therapy is tested for residual @-cell function. Why is C-peptide measured? [QIMS 25]

options.A: It reflects endogenous insulin secretion (not present in injected
options.B: It is unaffected by renal clearance insulin)
options.C: It is more potent than insulin
options.D: It is secreted in response to glucagon

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. C-peptide is released in equimolar amounts with endogenous insulin and has a longer half-life; low C-peptide with high insulin suggests exogenous insulin (factitious hypoglycaemia),. high both ￿ insulinoma/sulfonylurea.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old presents with vomiting, deep sighing respiration and f ruity breath. In which condition is ketoacidosis more common. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Absolute insulin deficiency + glucagon excess 4 lipolysis and hepatic ketogenesis (acetoacetate. F-hydroxybutyrate); type 2 more often gets hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state because some insulin suppresses ketogenesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic on insulin becomes hypoglycaemic. Which hormone rises in response to hypoglycaemia? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Counter-regulation: glucagon (first defence), adrenaline, then cortisol and GH. In long-standing type l DM the glucagon response is lost hypoglycaemia unawareness.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During prolonged fasting, a hormone drives both hepatic glycogen breakdown and ketone formation. Which hormone stimulates both ketogenesis and glycogenolysis. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucagon 4 cAMP/PKA 4 glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, I malonyl-CoA (via ACC inhibition) 4 CPT-I active ￿ F-oxidation and ketogenesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A thin 12~year-old with polyuria and weight loss has undetectable C-peptide and anti-GAD antibodies. What characterizes type I diabetes mellitus. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Absolute insulin deficiency from autoimmune F-cell destruction

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Type l DM: HLA-DR3/DR4. autoantibodies (GAD65, IA-2, insulin. ZnT8). insulin-dependent, ketosis-prone. Type 2: insulin resistance with relative deficiency, strong genetic and obesity links.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has fasted for 16 hours and glucagon is rising. Which change helps maintain hepatic glucose production. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gluconeogenic substrates: lactate (Cori cycle from RBCS and muscle), alanine (glucose-alanine cycle), glycerol (lipolysis), propionate. Acetyl-CoA cannot make net glucose but activates pyruvate carboxylase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A type I diabetic has vomiting, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, glucose 450 mg/dL, pH 7.10, bicarbonate 14 and positive ketones. What is the diagnosis. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DKA: hyperglycaemia + high anion gap metabolic acidosis + ketonaemia," total body K. depleted even if serum K. is high. Treat with fluids, insulin infusion and potassium.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, insulin rises. Which metabolic response does insulin cause. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Increased glycogen synthesis and fatty-acid synthesis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin (storage hormone): t glucose uptake (muscle, fat). glycogenesis, lipogenesis (activates ACC), protein synthesis; I glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, lipolysis (HSL), ketogenesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An a-cell tumour secretes excess glucagon. Which effect is most likely? [HITEC 26]

options.B: Hyperglycaemia from increased hepatic glucose production

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucagonoma: diabetes, necrolytic migratory erythema, weight loss, DVT; glucagon acts mainly on liver (no muscle receptors) - glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, ketogenesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a large IV dose of insulin for hyperkalaemia, recovery from hypoglycaemia is delayed. Which deficiency best explains this? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucagon is the first and most important counter-regulatory hormone (minutes); adrenaline is second; cortisol and GH act over hours.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares glucose uptake in different tissues. Insulin increases glucose entry into which tissue. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin-independent glucose uptake: brain (GLUT1/3), RBCS, liver (GLUT2), kidney, intestine, F-cells, lens. nerves (sorbitol accumulation in diabetes).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old obese man with type 2 diabetes has high fasting insulin but high blood glucose. What best explains this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Early type 2 DM: hyperinsulinaemia compensates for resistance: when F-cells fail, glucose rises despite high insulin; later insulin levels fall.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies regulation of ketogenesis. In which state does ketone-body production increase. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low insulin/high glucagon: lipolysis t (HSL), malonyl-CoA l ￿ CPT-I active 4 F-oxidation 4 acetyl-CoA 4 HMG-COA synthase (mitochondrial) ketones (liver cannot use them - lacks thiophorase).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a meal, insulin rises. Which process does insulin suppress. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin suppresses gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, lipolysis, ketogenesis and proteolysis; it stimulates glycogenesis, lipogenesis. protein synthesis and GLUT4-mediated uptake.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with a somatostatinoma has diabetes, gallstones and steatorrhoea. Besides GH, somatostatin also inhibits secretion of which hormone. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Somatostatin (6-cells, hypothalamus, gut D-cells) inhibits GH. TSH, insulin. glucagon. gastrin, secretin, CCK and pancreatic exocrine secretion - paracrine "brake" in the islets.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During an overnight fast, glucagon rises. Which hepatic processes does glucagon stimulate. [BWP 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucagon (liver only) 4 cAMP/PKA 4 phosphorylase activation, glycogen synthase inhibition, l F-2,6-BP (gluconeogenesis t ). PEPCK induction, I pyruvate kinase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with DKA (pH 7.05) is treated with insulin inf usion. How does insulin change blood pH in this setting. [BWP 26]

options.B: Increases blood pH by stopping ketogenesis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin halts lipolysis and ketone production and promotes ketone use 4 acidosis corrects (anion gap closes); it also drives K. into cells. Source item was ambiguous.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies insulin processing in F-cell granules. Which segment is removed from proinsulin to produce mature insulin? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prohormone convertases (PC1/3, PC2) and carboxypeptidase E excise C-peptide,. insulin A (21 aa) and B (30 aa) chains remain joined by two disulfide bonds. ENDOCRINOLOGY - MALE & FEMALE REPRODUCTIVE HORMONES

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old girl has acne and hirsutism from excess androgens. Which is the most potent androgen. [Prof 24. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 5a-reductase converts testosterone to DHT (binds the androgen receptor~2-3x more avidly) in prostate, skin and external genitalia. DHEA and androstenedione are weak adrenal androgens.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During pregnancy, maternal urinary estriol is used to assess fetal wellbeing. How is estriol mainly synthesized? [KIMS 26. AMC 25. BWP 25]

options.B: By the fetoplacental unit from fetal adrenal DHEA-S (16-hydroxylated in fetal liver)
options.C: By the maternal ovary from cholesterol

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Placenta lacks 17a-hydroxylase, so it uses fetal DHEA-S; estriol therefore reflects fetal adrenal, liver and placental function. Low estriol (with low hCG) suggests fetal compromise/death.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old woman has frequent back and joint pains; DEXA shows low bone density. What is the main cause of bone loss after menopause. [AMC 25]

options.B: Estrogen deficiency increasing osteoclastic resorption ( t RANKL, I OPG)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Options/key created.. the AMC 25 recall had the stem only. Estrogen increases osteoprotegerin and reduces RANKUIL-6. limiting osteoclast activity; its loss 4 postmenopausal (type l) osteoporosis, fractures of vertebrae and wrist.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with recurrent early miscarriages has a luteal phase defect with low progesterone. Which treatment supports the corpus luteum in early pregnancy. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corpus luteum needs hCG to secrete progesterone, which maintains the decidua and quietens the myometrium. Mifepristone (antiprogestin) induces abortion. Key note: source options were incomplete.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After menopause, estrogen replacement prevents progression of osteoporosis. What is the mechanism of its protective effect? [QIMS 25]

options.D: Stimulates osteoblast activity and restrains osteoclasts

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Estrogen promotes osteoblast activity and t OPG / I RANKL, reducing osteoclast formation and lifespan; loss of estrogen accelerates trabecular bone loss.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man has a weak stream and nocturia due to an enlarged prostate. Which enzyme activity is most directly responsible. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. DHT drives prostatic growth; finasteride (5a-reductase type 2 inhibitor) shrinks the prostate. 5a-reductase deficiency 4 ambiguous genitalia at birth with virilization at puberty.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 27-year-old woman with infertility has an aromatase gene mutation. Which change in ovarian steroid synthesis occurs. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increased conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone
options.B: Accumulation of androgens with decreased estrogen production

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Aromatase (CYP19, granulosa cells under FSH) converts androstenedione 4 estrone and testosterone estradiol. Two-cell theory: LH-stimulated theca make androgens; FSH-stimulated granulosa aromatize them.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has recurrent early pregnancy loss with luteal-phase progesterone deficiency. Which function of progesterone is impaired? [QIMS 25]

options.B: Maintenance of the secretory endometrium and suppression of uterine contractility

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key supplied: the source gave no answer key. Progesterone." secretory endometrium (glycogen glands), decidualization, myometrial quiescence, thick cervical mucus, thermogenic effect, breast alveolar development.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 46,XY infant has ambiguous external genitalia but normal internal male ducts. Which hormone is essential for development of the fetal male external genitalia. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Testosterone 4 Wolffian ducts (epididymis, vas, seminal vesicles)," DHT 4 penis, scrotum, urethra and prostate. 5a-reductase type 2 deficiency ambiguous genitalia, virilization at puberty.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with PCOS has acanthosis nigricans and obesity. PCOS is associated with an increased risk of which disease. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Type 2 diabetes mellitus due to insulin resistance

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin resistance with hyperinsulinaemia drives ovarian theca androgen production and I SHBG,. PCOS raises risk of type 2 DM, dyslipidaemia, endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; metformin is used.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A young woman has excess coarse hair on her face and chest. Hirsutism is due to excess of which hormones. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Androgen excess (PCOS commonest; CAH. androgen-secreting tumours, Cushing) converts vellus to terminal hair in androgen-dependent areas.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 46,XY infant has ambiguous genitalia due to an enzyme defect. What is the role of 5a-reductase in male sexual development? [BWP 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 5a-reductase type 2 (genital skin, prostate) makes DHT for external genitalia and prostate; deficiency 4 "penis at 12 (Guevedoces). Aromatase makes estradiol; 17F-HSD makes testosterone.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces testosterone synthesis in Leydig cells. Which precursor (among these) is the more immediate substrate for testosterone synthesis? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A5 pathway: pregnenolone 4 17-OH-pregnenolone ￿ DHEA ￿ androstenedione (3F-HSD) 4 testosterone (17F-HSD3). Androstenedione is the immediate precursor; DHEA is the closest among the options.
